sentences.zh: 齊武帝諸子文惠諸子明帝諸子

translations.literal: The Sons of Emperor Wu of Qi; the Sons of Wenhui; the Sons of Ming
translations.idiomatic: The Sons of Emperor Wu of Southern Qi; The Sons of Emperor Wenhui; The Sons of Emperor Ming

sentences.zh: 武帝二十三男：穆皇后生文惠太子、竟陵文宣王子良，張淑妃生廬陵王子卿、魚復侯子響，周淑儀生安陸王子敬、建安王子真，阮淑媛生晉安王子懋、衡陽王子峻，王淑儀生隨郡王子隆，蔡婕妤生西陽王子明，樂容華生南海王子罕，傅充華生巴陵王子倫，謝昭儀生邵陵王子貞，江淑儀生臨賀王子岳，庾昭容生西陽王子文，荀昭華生南康王子琳，顏婕妤生永陽王子瑉，宮人謝生湘東王子建，何充華生南郡王子夏。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu had twenty-three sons: Empress Mu bore the Crown Prince Wenhui and Xiao Ziliang, Prince Wenxuan of Jingling; Consort Zhang Shufei bore Xiao Ziqing, Prince of Luling, and Xiao Zixiang, Marquis of Yufu; Lady Zhou Shuyi bore Xiao Zijing, Prince of Anlu, and Xiao Zizhen, Prince of Jian'an; Lady Ruan Shuyuan bore Xiao Zimao, Prince of Jin'an, and Xiao Zijun, Prince of Hengyang; Lady Wang Shuyi bore Xiao Zilong, Prince of Suizhou; Lady Cai Jieyu bore Xiao Ziming, Prince of Xiyang; Lady Yue Ronghua bore Xiao Zihan, Prince of Nanhai; Lady Fu Chonghua bore Xiao Zilun, Prince of Baling; Lady Xie Zhaoyi bore Xiao Zizhen, Prince of Shaoling; Lady Jiang Shuyi bore Xiao Ziyue, Prince of Linhe; Lady Yu Zhaorong bore Xiao Ziwen, Prince of Xiyang; Lady Xun Zhaohua bore Xiao Zilin, Prince of Nankang; Lady Yan Jieyu bore Xiao Zimin, Prince of Yongyang; palace woman Xie bore Xiao Zijian, Prince of Xiangdong; Lady He Chonghua bore Xiao Zixia, Prince of Nanjun.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu had twenty-three sons. Empress Mu gave birth to the Crown Prince Wenhui and to Xiao Ziliang, Prince Wenxuan of Jingling. Consort Zhang Shufei bore Xiao Ziqing, Prince of Luling, and Xiao Zixiang, Marquis of Yufu. Lady Zhou Shuyi bore Xiao Zijing, Prince of Anlu, and Xiao Zizhen, Prince of Jian'an. Lady Ruan Shuyuan bore Xiao Zimao, Prince of Jin'an, and Xiao Zijun, Prince of Hengyang. Lady Wang Shuyi bore Xiao Zilong, Prince of Suizhou. Lady Cai Jieyu bore Xiao Ziming, Prince of Xiyang. Lady Yue Ronghua bore Xiao Zihan, Prince of Nanhai. Lady Fu Chonghua bore Xiao Zilun, Prince of Baling. Lady Xie Zhaoyi bore Xiao Zizhen, Prince of Shaoling. Lady Jiang Shuyi bore Xiao Ziyue, Prince of Linhe. Lady Yu Zhaorong bore Xiao Ziwen, Prince of Xiyang. Lady Xun Zhaohua bore Xiao Zilin, Prince of Nankang. Lady Yan Jieyu bore Xiao Zimin, Prince of Yongyang. A palace woman surnamed Xie bore Xiao Zijian, Prince of Xiangdong, and Lady He Chonghua bore Xiao Zixia, Prince of Nanjun.

sentences.zh: 第六、第十二、第十五、第二十二皇子早亡；

translations.literal: The sixth, twelfth, fifteenth, and twenty-second princes died young;
translations.idiomatic: The sixth, twelfth, fifteenth, and twenty-second princes died in childhood;

sentences.zh: 子瑉繼衡陽元王后。

translations.literal: Zimin succeeded as king after the original Queen of Hengyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zimin succeeded to the line of the late Queen of Hengyang.

sentences.zh: 文惠皇太子長懋，字雲喬，小字白澤，武帝長子也。

translations.literal: The Crown Prince Wenhui, Changmao, whose style name was Yunqiao and childhood name Baize, was Emperor Wu's eldest son.
translations.idiomatic: The Crown Prince Wenhui, Xiao Changmao—style name Yunqiao, childhood name Baize—was Emperor Wu's eldest son.

sentences.zh: 武帝年未弱冠而生太子，姿容豐美，為高帝所愛。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu was not yet twenty when the crown prince was born; his appearance was full and beautiful, and he was loved by Emperor Gao.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu was still under twenty when the crown prince was born. The boy's looks were strikingly handsome, and Emperor Gao doted on him.

sentences.zh: 宋元徽末，除秘書郎，不拜，板輔國將軍，遷晉熙王撫軍主簿。

translations.literal: At the end of the Song Yuanhui era he was appointed Secretary Gentleman but did not accept the post; he was commissioned as General Who Assists the State and transferred to be Registrar on the staff of the Prince of Jinxi's Pacification Army.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Song Yuanhui reign, he was named Secretary Gentleman but declined the appointment. He was then commissioned as General Who Assists the State and appointed Registrar on the staff of the Prince of Jinxi's Pacification Army.

sentences.zh: 事甯，武帝遣太子還都。

translations.literal: When matters were settled in Ning, Emperor Wu sent the crown prince back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Once affairs in Ning were settled, Emperor Wu sent the crown prince back to the capital.

sentences.zh: 高帝方創霸業，心存嫡嗣，謂太子曰：「汝還，吾事辦矣。

translations.literal: Emperor Gao was then founding his hegemony and kept the legitimate heir in mind; he told the crown prince, "When you return, my task will be accomplished.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gao was then laying the foundations of his rule and kept the legitimate heir firmly in mind. He told the crown prince, "Once you are back, my work here is done.

sentences.zh: 」處之府東齋，令通文武賓客。

translations.literal: " He lodged him in the eastern study of the princely residence and had him receive civil and military guests.
translations.idiomatic: " He housed him in the eastern study of the princely residence and allowed him to receive both civil and military retainers.

sentences.zh: 謂荀伯玉曰：「我出行日，城中軍悉受長懋節度。

translations.literal: He said to Xun Boyu, "On the day I go out, all troops in the city shall be under Changmao's command.
translations.idiomatic: He told Xun Boyu, "On any day I am away, every soldier in the city is to answer to Changmao's orders.

sentences.zh: 我雖不行，內外直防及諸門甲兵，悉令長懋時時履行。」

translations.literal: Even when I do not go out, have Changmao inspect from time to time the inner and outer guards on duty and the armored troops at every gate."
translations.idiomatic: Even when I stay in, have Changmao inspect the inner and outer guards on duty and the armored troops at every gate on a regular basis."

sentences.zh: 轉秘書丞，以與宣帝諱同，不就。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be Secretary Director, but because this title shared a character with Emperor Xuan's tabooed name he did not take the post.
translations.idiomatic: He was next appointed Secretary Director, but because the title shared a character with Emperor Xuan's tabooed name he declined the office.

sentences.zh: 曆中書、黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: He successively served as Central Secretariat Attendant and Gentleman Attendant at the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as Central Secretariat Attendant and as Gentleman Attendant at the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 升明三年，高帝將受禪，以襄陽兵馬重鎮，不欲處他族，出太子為雍州刺史，加都督、北中郎將、甯蠻校尉。

translations.literal: In the third year of Shengming, as Emperor Gao was about to receive the abdication, because Xiangyang was a key post for troops and horses and he did not wish to place it in another clan's hands, he sent the crown prince out as Inspector of Yongzhou, with additional titles as Area Commander, General of the North Center, and Colonel Pacifying the Man.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Shengming, as Emperor Gao prepared to accept the abdication, he posted the crown prince to Yongzhou as inspector—with additional titles as area commander, General of the North Center, and Colonel Pacifying the Man—because Xiangyang was a vital military center and he did not want it held by any other house.

sentences.zh: 建元元年，封南郡王，江左嫡皇孫封王，始自此也。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jianyuan he was enfeoffed as Prince of Nanjun; from this time began the enfeoffment as prince of legitimate imperial grandsons south of the Yangzi.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jianyuan he was enfeoffed as Prince of Nanjun—the first time south of the Yangzi that a legitimate imperial grandson had been made a prince.

sentences.zh: 先是，梁州刺史范柏年頗著威名，沈攸之事起，候望形勢，事平，朝廷遣王玄邈代之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Fan Bonian, Inspector of Liangzhou, had enjoyed considerable renown; when Shen Youzhi's rebellion arose he watched how matters developed, and after it was pacified the court sent Wang Xuanmiao to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Fan Bonian, inspector of Liangzhou, had built a considerable reputation. When Shen Youzhi's rebellion broke out he watched which way the wind was blowing; after the revolt was crushed the court sent Wang Xuanmiao to replace him.

sentences.zh: 玄邈已至，柏年遲回魏興不肯下，太子慮其為變，乃遣說之，許啟為府長史。

translations.literal: When Xuanmiao had already arrived, Bonian lingered at Weixing and refused to step down; the crown prince, fearing he might stir up trouble, sent envoys to persuade him and promised to recommend him as Chief Clerk of the princely staff.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanmiao had already arrived, but Fan lingered at Weixing and refused to yield his post. Fearing a coup, the crown prince sent envoys to win him over, promising to recommend him as chief clerk of the princely staff.

sentences.zh: 及至襄陽，因執誅之。

translations.literal: When Bonian reached Xiangyang, he was seized and executed.
translations.idiomatic: Once Fan reached Xiangyang, he was seized and put to death.

sentences.zh: 二年，徵為侍中、中軍將軍，置府，鎮石頭。

translations.literal: In the second year he was summoned as Palace Attendant and General of the Central Army, with a staff established, and garrisoned at Stone City.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was recalled to serve as Palace Attendant and General of the Central Army, with his own staff, and was posted to garrison Stone City.

sentences.zh: 穆妃薨，成服日，車駕出臨喪，朝議疑太子應出門迎。

translations.literal: When Consort Mu died, on the day of assuming mourning garb the imperial carriage went out to attend the mourning; court opinion was uncertain whether the crown prince should go out to welcome it.
translations.idiomatic: When Consort Mu died, on the day the crown prince donned mourning garb the emperor himself came to the funeral. Court opinion was divided over whether the crown prince ought to go out and receive him.

sentences.zh: 左僕射王儉曰：「尋禮記服問：'君所主夫人、妻、太子嫡婦。

translations.literal: Left Vice Director Wang Jian said, "Consulting the 'Questions on Mourning' in the Book of Rites: 'The ruler presides over mourning for his lady, his wife, and the crown prince's principal consort.'
translations.idiomatic: Left Vice Director Wang Jian argued, "The 'Questions on Mourning' in the Book of Rites states: 'The ruler presides over mourning for his lady, his wife, and the crown prince's principal consort.'

sentences.zh: '言國君為此三人為主喪也。

translations.literal: ' This means the ruler presides over mourning for these three persons.
translations.idiomatic: That is to say, it is the ruler who presides over mourning for these three.

sentences.zh: 今鑾輿臨降，自以主喪而至，雖因事撫慰，義不在吊，南郡以下不應出門奉迎。

translations.literal: Now that the imperial carriage has come down, it comes in its capacity as presiding mourner; although it may offer consolation in passing, by rite it is not coming to offer condolence, and those below the Prince of Nanjun should not go out to welcome it.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial carriage has come down now precisely as presiding mourner. Though the visit may bring comfort in passing, by rite it is not a condolence call, and no one below the Prince of Nanjun should go out to receive it.

sentences.zh: 但尊極所臨，禮有變革，權去杖絰，移立戶外，足表情敬，無煩止哭。

translations.literal: Yet when the supreme sovereign arrives, rites may be altered; one may provisionally set aside staff and mourning sash and stand outside the door—enough to show respect in feeling, without need to stop weeping.
translations.idiomatic: When the supreme sovereign himself appears, however, ritual may be adjusted: lay aside staff and sash for the moment and stand outside the door—enough to show respect without requiring an end to weeping.

sentences.zh: 皇太子既一宮之主，自應以車駕幸宮，依常奉候。

translations.literal: Since the crown prince is master of his own palace, the imperial carriage should come to the palace in the usual way of attendance.
translations.idiomatic: As master of his own palace, the crown prince should receive the imperial visit there in the ordinary manner.

sentences.zh: 既當成服之日，吉凶不相干，宜以衰幘行事，望拜止哭，率由舊章。

translations.literal: Since this is the day for assuming mourning garb, auspicious and inauspicious matters do not interfere with each other; he should act wearing the mourning cap and headband, gaze toward the visitor and bow, then cease weeping—all according to established precedent.
translations.idiomatic: On the day one assumes full mourning, auspicious and inauspicious rites do not clash. He should wear the mourning cap and headband, bow toward the visitor from where he stands, then cease weeping—all as precedent dictates.

sentences.zh: 尊駕不以臨吊，奉迎則惟常體，求之情禮，如為可安。

translations.literal: The imperial visit is not a condolence call; to receive it in the usual manner accords with feeling and rite and seems acceptable.
translations.idiomatic: The sovereign is not coming to offer formal condolence; receiving him in the usual way satisfies both feeling and rite and seems the sound course.

sentences.zh: 」又其年九月有閏，小祥疑應計閏。

translations.literal: " Moreover, that year had an intercalary ninth month, and there was doubt whether the small felicitations mourning should count the intercalary month.
translations.idiomatic: " That year also had an intercalary ninth month, raising the question of whether the small-felicitations mourning period should include the intercalary month.

sentences.zh: 儉又議，以為「三百六旬，尚書明義，文公納幣，春秋致譏。

translations.literal: Jian again argued that "three hundred and sixty days" is the clear meaning in the Documents; when Duke Wen accepted betrothal gifts, the Spring and Autumn Annals censured him.
translations.idiomatic: Jian argued further that "three hundred and sixty days" is the clear meaning given in the Documents, and that when Duke Wen of Jin accepted betrothal gifts the Spring and Autumn Annals censured him for it.

sentences.zh: 故先儒期喪，歲數沒閏，大功以下，月數數閏。

translations.literal: Therefore the early Confucians held that for the one-year mourning the year-count absorbs the intercalary month, while for mourning below the great-achievement grade the month-count counts the intercalary month.
translations.idiomatic: The early Confucians therefore held that for one-year mourning the year-count absorbs the intercalary month, whereas for mourning below the great-achievement grade the month-count includes it.

sentences.zh: 所以吳商云：'含閏以正期，允協情理。

translations.literal: Hence Wu Shang said, 'Including the intercalary month to fix the term of mourning accords with reason and feeling.
translations.idiomatic: That is why Wu Shang wrote, 'Counting the intercalary month to fix the mourning term accords with both reason and feeling.

sentences.zh: '沒閏之理，固在言先」。

translations.literal: ' The principle of absorbing the intercalary month is already stated beforehand."
translations.idiomatic: The principle of absorbing the intercalary month is already set forth in the earlier texts.'"

sentences.zh: 並從之。

translations.literal: All followed his views.
translations.idiomatic: The court adopted all of his recommendations.

sentences.zh: 永明三年，於崇正殿講孝經，少傅王儉令太子僕周顒撰為義疏。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yongming, at Chongzheng Hall he lectured on the Classic of Filial Piety; Junior Tutor Wang Jian had the crown prince's steward Zhou Yong compile an expository commentary.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yongming he lectured on the Classic of Filial Piety at Chongzheng Hall; Junior Tutor Wang Jian had the crown prince's steward Zhou Yong compile an expository commentary.

sentences.zh: 五年冬，太子臨國學，親臨策試諸生，於坐問少傅王儉曲禮云：「無不敬。

translations.literal: In the winter of the fifth year the crown prince visited the Imperial Academy and personally presided over written examinations of the students; seated there he asked Junior Tutor Wang Jian about the Ceremonies: "There is nothing that is not to be respected.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the fifth year the crown prince visited the Imperial Academy and personally presided over the written examinations. From his seat he asked Junior Tutor Wang Jian about a passage in the Ceremonies: "There is nothing that is not to be respected.

sentences.zh: 」義，儉及竟陵王子良等各有酬答。

translations.literal: " On its meaning, Jian and Xiao Ziliang of Jingling and others each gave replies.
translations.idiomatic: " On its meaning, Jian, Xiao Ziliang of Jingling, and the others each offered replies.

sentences.zh: 太子又以此義問諸學生，謝幾卿等一十人，並以筆對。

translations.literal: The crown prince also put this question to the students; Xie Jiqing and ten others all answered in writing.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince put the same question to the students; Xie Jiqing and ten others all answered in writing.

sentences.zh: 太子問王儉：「周易幹卦本施天位，而說卦雲'帝出乎震'，震本非天義，豈當相主？

translations.literal: The crown prince asked Wang Jian, "In the Book of Changes the Qian hexagram originally assigns Heaven's position, yet the Explanation of the Trigrams says 'The Emperor emerges from Zhen'; Zhen by nature is not Heaven's meaning—should they preside over each other?
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince asked Wang Jian, "In the Book of Changes the Qian hexagram assigns Heaven its place, yet the Explanation of the Trigrams says, 'The Emperor emerges from Zhen.' Zhen is not Heaven by nature—how can the two preside over each other?

sentences.zh: 」儉曰：「幹健震動，天以運為德，故言'帝出乎震。

translations.literal: " Jian said, "Qian is firm and Zhen is stirring; Heaven takes movement as its virtue, hence it says 'The Emperor emerges from Zhen.'
translations.idiomatic: " Jian replied, "Qian is firm and Zhen is stirring. Heaven takes movement as its virtue, which is why the text says, 'The Emperor emerges from Zhen.'

sentences.zh: 」儉又諮太子孝經「仲尼居曾子侍。

translations.literal: " Jian also questioned the crown prince on the Classic of Filial Piety passage "Confucius was at home and Zengzi attended him.
translations.idiomatic: " Jian also questioned the crown prince on the Classic of Filial Piety: "Confucius was at home and Zengzi attended him.

sentences.zh: 」義，臨川王映諮「孝為德本。

translations.literal: " On its meaning; the Prince of Linchuan, Xiao Ying, questioned him on "Filial piety is the root of virtue.
translations.idiomatic: " On its meaning. The Prince of Linchuan, Xiao Ying, questioned him on "Filial piety is the root of virtue.

sentences.zh: 」義，太子並應機酬答，甚有條貫。

translations.literal: " On its meaning; the crown prince answered each on the spot with great coherence.
translations.idiomatic: " On its meaning. The crown prince answered each question on the spot with notable coherence.

sentences.zh: 明年，上將訊丹陽所領囚及南北二百里內獄，詔太子于玄圃園宣猷堂錄三署囚，原宥各有差。

translations.literal: The next year, as the emperor was about to review prisoners under Danyang's jurisdiction and prisons within two hundred li north and south, he ordered the crown prince at Xuanyou Hall in the Mystic Orchard to record prisoners of the three bureaus and grant pardons in varying degrees.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, as the emperor prepared to review prisoners under Danyang's jurisdiction and every jail within two hundred li to the north and south, he ordered the crown prince to record the prisoners of the three bureaus at Xuanyou Hall in the Mystic Orchard and grant pardons in varying degrees.

sentences.zh: 上晚年好游宴，尚書曹事，亦分送太子省視。

translations.literal: In his later years the emperor delighted in feasting and excursions; matters of the Secretariat offices were also sent in part to the crown prince for review.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years the emperor delighted in feasting and excursions, and even Secretariat business was partly forwarded to the crown prince for review.

sentences.zh: 太子與竟陵王子良俱好釋氏，立六疾館以養窮人。

translations.literal: The crown prince and Xiao Ziliang of Jingling both favored Buddhism and established the Six Diseases Hall to support the destitute.
translations.idiomatic: Both the crown prince and Xiao Ziliang of Jingling were devoted to Buddhism and founded the Six Diseases Hall to care for the destitute.

sentences.zh: 而性頗奢麗，宮內殿堂，皆雕飾精綺，過於上宮。

translations.literal: Yet by nature he was rather extravagant; the halls within his palace were all carved and adorned with fine brocade, surpassing the upper palace.
translations.idiomatic: By nature, however, he was extravagantly fond of display: every hall in his palace was carved and hung with fine brocade, outdoing even the emperor's own quarters.

sentences.zh: 開拓玄圃園與台城北塹等，其中起出土山池閣樓觀塔宇，窮奇極麗，費以千萬。

translations.literal: He expanded the Mystic Orchard to equal the northern moat of the terrace city; within it he raised earthen mountains, ponds, pavilions, towers, belvederes, and pagodas to the utmost wonder and beauty, at a cost of tens of millions.
translations.idiomatic: He expanded the Mystic Orchard until it matched the northern moat of the terrace city, raising within it artificial hills, ponds, pavilions, towers, belvederes, and pagodas of the utmost wonder and splendor at a cost of tens of millions.

sentences.zh: 多聚異石，妙極山水。

translations.literal: He gathered many strange stones and achieved the utmost artistry in landscape.
translations.idiomatic: He collected rare stones and shaped landscapes of extraordinary refinement.

sentences.zh: 慮上宮中望見，乃旁列修竹，外施高鄣。

translations.literal: Fearing the upper palace might see it, he planted tall bamboo along the sides and set up high screens outside.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing the view from the upper palace, he planted tall bamboo along the perimeter and erected high screens outside.

sentences.zh: 造遊牆數百間，施諸機巧，宜須鄣蔽，須臾成立，若應毀撤，應手遷徙。

translations.literal: He built several hundred sections of touring walls fitted with all manner of ingenious devices; when screens were needed they were set up in an instant, and if they were to be taken down they could be moved away at a touch.
translations.idiomatic: He built several hundred sections of touring wall fitted with ingenious mechanisms: screens could be raised in an instant when needed and dismantled or shifted at a touch.

sentences.zh: 制珍玩之物，織孔雀毛為裘，光採金翠，過於雉頭遠矣。

translations.literal: He fashioned rare curios, weaving peacock feathers into fur robes whose luster of gold and kingfisher green far surpassed pheasant-head brocade.
translations.idiomatic: Among his rare curios were fur robes woven from peacock feathers, their gold-and-emerald luster far surpassing even pheasant-head brocade.

sentences.zh: 以晉明帝為太子時立西池，乃啟武帝引前例，求于東田起小苑，上許之。

translations.literal: Because when Emperor Ming of Jin was crown prince he had established the Western Pond, he memorialized Emperor Wu citing this precedent and requested to build a small garden in the Eastern Fields; the emperor granted it.
translations.idiomatic: Citing the precedent of Emperor Ming of Jin, who as crown prince had built the Western Pond, he petitioned Emperor Wu for permission to lay out a small garden in the Eastern Fields, and the emperor granted it.

sentences.zh: 永明中，二宮兵力全實，太子使宮中將吏更番築役，營城包巷，制度之盛，觀者傾都。

translations.literal: During Yongming, the military strength of both palaces was at full strength; the crown prince had officers and clerks of the palace take turns at construction labor, building walls that enclosed whole lanes—the scale of the works made the whole capital gaze in wonder.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yongming era both palaces were at full military strength. The crown prince set palace officers and clerks to construction duty in rotating shifts, building walls that enclosed whole lanes on a scale that left the capital staring in astonishment.

sentences.zh: 上性雖嚴，太子所為，無敢啟者。

translations.literal: Although the emperor's nature was strict, no one dared report what the crown prince was doing.
translations.idiomatic: Strict though the emperor's temper was, no one dared report what the crown prince was doing.

sentences.zh: 後上幸豫章王宅，還過太子東田，見其彌亙華遠，壯麗極目，於是大怒，收監作主帥，太子懼，皆藏之，由是見責。

translations.literal: Later, when the emperor visited the Prince of Yuzhang's residence and on returning passed the crown prince's Eastern Fields, he saw how they stretched on in splendor to the horizon; he was greatly angered, seized and imprisoned the supervising officers, and the crown prince in fear hid everything away—thereby incurring rebuke.
translations.idiomatic: Later, returning from a visit to the Prince of Yuzhang's residence, the emperor passed the crown prince's Eastern Fields and saw splendor stretching to the horizon. He flew into a rage, seized and imprisoned the supervising officers, and the crown prince, terrified, hid everything away—earning a sharp rebuke.

sentences.zh: 太子素疾，體又過壯，常在宮內，簡於遨遊，玩弄羽儀，多所僭擬。

translations.literal: The crown prince had long been ill, yet his physique was overly robust; he usually remained within the palace, sparing himself excursions, and in handling insignia often overstepped what was permitted.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince had long been in poor health, yet his physique was unusually robust. He rarely left the palace or went on excursions, but in handling ceremonial insignia he often exceeded what was permitted.

sentences.zh: 雖咫尺宮禁，而上終不知。

translations.literal: Though the palace precincts were only a short distance away, the emperor to the end did not know.
translations.idiomatic: Though the imperial quarters were only steps away, the emperor never found out.

sentences.zh: 又使徐文景造輦及乘輿禦物虎賁雲罕之屬，上嘗幸東宮，匆匆不暇藏輦，文景乃以佛像內輦中，故上不疑。

translations.literal: He also had Xu Wenjing make imperial carriages and regalia such as tiger guards and cloud canopies; once when the emperor visited the Eastern Palace there was no time to hide the carriage, so Wenjing placed Buddhist images inside it, and thus the emperor did not suspect.
translations.idiomatic: He also had Xu Wenjing construct imperial carriages and regalia—the tiger guards, cloud canopies, and the like. Once, when the emperor visited the Eastern Palace in haste, there was no time to hide a carriage; Wenjing stuffed Buddhist images inside it, and the emperor suspected nothing.

sentences.zh: 文景父陶仁時為給事中，謂文景曰：「終當滅門，政當掃墓待喪耳。

translations.literal: Wenjing's father Tao Ren was then a Supervising Attendant Within the Palace and said to Wenjing, "In the end our whole clan will be destroyed; we should just sweep the graves and wait for the mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Wenjing's father Tao Ren, then a Supervising Attendant Within the Palace, told him, "This will end in the destruction of our whole clan. We might as well sweep the graves and wait for the funeral.

sentences.zh: 」及移家避之。

translations.literal: " He then moved his family away to avoid it.
translations.idiomatic: " He then moved his family away to escape the coming disaster.

sentences.zh: 其後文景竟賜死，陶仁遂不哭，時人以為有古人風。

translations.literal: Later Wenjing was indeed ordered to die by suicide; Tao Ren then did not weep, and people of the time thought this showed the spirit of the ancients.
translations.idiomatic: Wenjing was eventually ordered to take his own life. Tao Ren did not weep, and contemporaries took this as the spirit of the ancients.

sentences.zh: 十年，豫章王嶷薨，太子見上友于既至，造碑文奏之，未及鐫勒。

translations.literal: In the tenth year the Prince of Yuzhang, Xiao Yi, died; the crown prince, seeing the emperor's brotherly affection had reached its depth, composed an epitaph and presented it, but it had not yet been carved.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year the Prince of Yuzhang, Xiao Yi, died. Seeing how deeply the emperor mourned his brother, the crown prince composed an epitaph and submitted it, though it had not yet been carved in stone.

sentences.zh: 十一年春正月，太子有疾，上自臨視，有憂色。

translations.literal: In the first month of spring in the eleventh year the crown prince fell ill; the emperor came in person to visit him, his face showing worry.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of spring in the eleventh year the crown prince fell ill. The emperor came in person to see him, worry written on his face.

sentences.zh: 疾篤，上表告辭，薨於東宮崇明殿，時年三十六。

translations.literal: When his illness became critical he submitted a memorial of farewell and died at Chongming Hall in the Eastern Palace, aged thirty-six.
translations.idiomatic: When his illness turned critical he submitted a farewell memorial and died at Chongming Hall in the Eastern Palace, aged thirty-six.

sentences.zh: 武帝履行東宮，見太子服玩過制，大怒，敕有司隨事毀除，以東田殿堂處為崇虛館。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu walked through the Eastern Palace and, seeing the crown prince's garments and curios exceeded regulations, was greatly angered and ordered the authorities to destroy them item by item; the halls of the Eastern Fields were turned into the Lodge of Reverent Emptiness.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu toured the Eastern Palace and, finding the crown prince's garments and curios far beyond what regulations allowed, flew into a rage and ordered officials to destroy them one by one. The halls of the Eastern Fields were converted into the Lodge of Reverent Emptiness.

sentences.zh: 郁林立，追尊為文帝，廟稱世宗。

translations.literal: When the heir apparent was established, he was posthumously honored as Emperor Wen, with the temple name Shizong.
translations.idiomatic: When the heir apparent was installed, Changmao was posthumously honored as Emperor Wen, with the temple name Shizong.

sentences.zh: 初，太子惡明帝，密謂竟陵王子良曰：「我意色中殊不悅此人，當由其福德薄所致。

translations.literal: Earlier the crown prince disliked Emperor Ming and secretly told Xiao Ziliang of Jingling, "In my expression I am especially displeased with this man; it must be because his fortune and virtue are thin.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the crown prince had disliked Emperor Ming and confided to Xiao Ziliang of Jingling, "Something in this man's face fills me with distaste—it must be because his store of fortune and virtue is thin.

sentences.zh: 」子良便苦救解，後明帝立，果大相誅害。

translations.literal: " Ziliang then strenuously pleaded on his behalf; later, when Ming came to the throne, he indeed carried out great executions.
translations.idiomatic: " Ziliang pleaded strenuously on Ming's behalf. When Ming later took the throne, he carried out wholesale executions after all.

sentences.zh: 竟陵文宣王子良字雲英，武帝第二子也。

translations.literal: Xiao Ziliang, Prince Wenxuan of Jingling, whose style name was Yunying, was Emperor Wu's second son.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Ziliang, Prince Wenxuan of Jingling—style name Yunying—was Emperor Wu's second son.

sentences.zh: 幼聰敏。

translations.literal: As a child he was clever and quick.
translations.idiomatic: Even as a child he was exceptionally quick-witted.

sentences.zh: 武帝為贛縣時，與裴後不諧，遣人船送後還都，已登路，子良時年小，在庭前不悅。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu was magistrate of Gan County he was at odds with Consort Pei and sent her back to the capital by boat; she had already set out on the road when Ziliang, still young, stood in the courtyard displeased.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu was magistrate of Gan County he quarreled with Consort Pei and sent her back to the capital by boat. She had already embarked when the young Ziliang, standing in the courtyard, showed his displeasure plainly.

sentences.zh: 帝謂曰：「汝何不讀書？

translations.literal: The emperor said to him, "Why do you not study?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Why aren't you studying?

sentences.zh: 」子良曰：「娘今何處？

translations.literal: " Ziliang said, "Where is Mother now?
translations.idiomatic: " Ziliang replied, "Where is Mother now?

sentences.zh: 何用讀書。

translations.literal: What use is studying.
translations.idiomatic: What good is studying.

sentences.zh: 」帝異之，即召後還縣。

translations.literal: " The emperor was struck by this and at once summoned the consort back to the county.
translations.idiomatic: " Struck by the answer, the emperor at once recalled his consort to the county.

sentences.zh: 仕宋為邵陵王友。

translations.literal: Under the Song he served as Companion to the Prince of Shaoling.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Song he served as Companion to the Prince of Shaoling.

sentences.zh: 時宋道衰謝，諸王微弱，故不廢此官。

translations.literal: At that time the Song way was declining and princes were weak, so this office was not abolished.
translations.idiomatic: By then the Song house was in decline and its princes had little power, so the office was left in place.

sentences.zh: 升明三年，為會稽太守，都督五郡。

translations.literal: In the third year of Shengming he became Administrator of Kuaiji and Area Commander of five commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Shengming he was appointed Administrator of Kuaiji and area commander over five commanderies.

sentences.zh: 封聞喜公。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed as Duke of Wenxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed as Duke of Wenxi.

sentences.zh: 宋元嘉中，凡事皆責成郡縣，孝武后，徵求急速，以郡縣遲緩，始遣台使，自此公役勞擾。

translations.literal: During the Song Yuanjia era all matters were charged to the commanderies and counties; after Emperor Xiaowu, levies grew urgent, and because commanderies and counties were slow, palace envoys were first dispatched—from this time public labor and exactions became burdensome.
translations.idiomatic: During the Song Yuanjia era every task was pushed down to the commanderies and counties. After Emperor Xiaowu, levies grew ever more urgent; because local governments were slow to comply, the court began dispatching palace envoys—and from that point public labor and exactions became a constant burden.

sentences.zh: 高帝踐阼，子良陳之，請息其弊。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gao ascended the throne, Ziliang presented a memorial on this and requested that the abuse be stopped.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gao took the throne, Ziliang memorialized on the practice and asked that the abuse be ended.

sentences.zh: 子良敦義愛古，郡人朱百年有至行，先卒，賜其妻米百斛，蠲一人，給其薪蘇。

translations.literal: Ziliang was earnest in righteousness and loved antiquity; a man of the commandery, Zhu Bainian, had supreme conduct but had died earlier; he granted his wife a hundred hu of grain, exempted one person from labor, and supplied her fuel.
translations.idiomatic: Ziliang was earnest in righteousness and devoted to antiquity. Zhu Bainian of the commandery, a man of supreme moral conduct, had died earlier; Ziliang granted his widow a hundred hu of grain, exempted one person from labor on her behalf, and supplied her with fuel.

sentences.zh: 郡合下有虞翻舊床，罷任還，乃致以歸。

translations.literal: In the commandery headquarters there was an old couch of Yu Fan; when he left office and returned, he had it sent back to its home.
translations.idiomatic: In the commandery headquarters stood an old couch that had belonged to Yu Fan. When Ziliang left office he had it sent back to Yu's descendants.

sentences.zh: 後於西邸起古齋，多聚古人器服以充之。

translations.literal: Later at his western residence he built an Ancient Study and gathered many ancient vessels and garments to fill it.
translations.idiomatic: Later, at his western residence, he built an Ancient Study and filled it with antiquities—vessels, garments, and the like.

sentences.zh: 夏禹廟盛有禱祀，子良曰：「禹泣辜表仁，菲食旌約，服玩果粽，足以致誠。

translations.literal: The Temple of Yu the Great had lavish prayers and sacrifices; Ziliang said, "Yu wept over the guilty to show benevolence and ate sparingly to display restraint; fruit and rice dumplings as offerings are enough to show sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: The Temple of Yu the Great was given to lavish prayer and sacrifice. Ziliang said, "Yu wept over the guilty to show benevolence and ate sparingly to display restraint. Fruit and rice dumplings are offering enough to show sincerity.

sentences.zh: 」使歲獻扇簟而已。

translations.literal: " He had only fans and mats presented each year.
translations.idiomatic: " He ordered only fans and mats presented each year.

sentences.zh: 時有山陰人孔平詣子良訟嫂市米負錢不還。

translations.literal: At that time a man of Shanyin, Kong Ping, came before Ziliang to sue his sister-in-law for not repaying money owed for rice she had sold him.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Kong Ping of Shanyin came before Ziliang to sue his sister-in-law for failing to repay money owed on rice she had sold him.

sentences.zh: 子良歎曰：「昔高文通與寡嫂訟田，義異於此。

translations.literal: Ziliang sighed and said, "In the past Gao Wentong sued his widowed sister-in-law over fields—the righteousness was different from this.
translations.idiomatic: Ziliang sighed and said, "Long ago Gao Wentong sued his widowed sister-in-law over fields—a very different sort of righteousness from this.

sentences.zh: 」乃賜米錢以償平。

translations.literal: " He then granted grain and money to repay Ping.
translations.idiomatic: " He then granted grain and money to settle Ping's claim.

sentences.zh: 建元二年，穆妃薨，去官，仍為丹陽尹，開私倉振屬縣貧人。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianyuan Consort Mu died; he left office but continued as Administrator of Danyang, opening his private granary to relieve the poor of subordinate counties.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jianyuan Consort Mu died. Ziliang left office but continued as Administrator of Danyang, opening his private granary to relieve the poor of the subordinate counties.

sentences.zh: 先是太妃以七月薨，子良以八月奉凶問。

translations.literal: Earlier the princess consort had died in the seventh month; Ziliang announced the death in the eighth month.
translations.idiomatic: The princess consort had died in the seventh month; Ziliang announced the death in the eighth.

sentences.zh: 及小祥，疑南郡王應相待。

translations.literal: At the small felicitations mourning there was doubt whether the Prince of Nanjun should wait for him.
translations.idiomatic: At the small-felicitations mourning, court opinion was divided over whether the Prince of Nanjun ought to wait for him.

sentences.zh: 尚書左僕射王儉議以為「禮有倫序，義無徒設。

translations.literal: Left Vice Director of the Secretariat Wang Jian argued that "rites have an order of precedence and meaning is not set up in vain.
translations.idiomatic: Left Vice Director Wang Jian argued that "rites have an order of precedence; their meaning is never arbitrary.

sentences.zh: 如令遠則不待，近必相須，禮例既乖，即心無取。

translations.literal: If those far apart need not wait while those near must depend on each other, the ritual precedent is already at odds and the heart has no basis for acceptance.
translations.idiomatic: If the distant need not wait while the near must always coordinate, precedent is already violated and the heart has no ground for accepting the rule.

sentences.zh: 若疑兄弟同居，吉凶舛雜，則遠還之子，自應開立別門，以終喪事，靈筵祭奠，隨在家之人，再期而毀。

translations.literal: If one doubts that brothers dwelling together mix auspicious and inauspicious affairs, then a son returning from afar should open a separate gate to complete mourning; offerings at the spirit altar follow those at home, and after two years the mourning hall is destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: If one fears that brothers under one roof will mix auspicious and inauspicious rites, a son returning from afar should set up a separate mourning gate and complete his observances there; offerings at the spirit altar follow whoever remains at home, and the mourning hall is dismantled after two years.

sentences.zh: 庶子在家，亦不待嫡。

translations.literal: A secondary son at home also does not wait for the principal son.
translations.idiomatic: A secondary son at home does not wait for the principal heir either.

sentences.zh: 而況儲妃正體王室，中軍長嫡之重，天朝又行權制，進退彌復非疑。

translations.literal: How much more when the stored consort is the legitimate body of the royal house and the Central Army bears the weight of the eldest legitimate son—the court moreover exercises discretionary rites, so advance and retreat are all the less doubtful.
translations.idiomatic: How much more when the stored consort is the legitimate consort of the royal house and the Central Army bears the weight of the eldest legitimate son—especially when the court is already exercising discretionary rites. Under such circumstances advance and retreat are scarcely in doubt.

sentences.zh: 謂應不相待，中軍祥縞之日，聞喜致哀而已，不受吊慰。

translations.literal: He held that they should not wait for each other; on the day the Central Army donned felicitations mourning garb, Wenxi need only offer condolences and should not receive condolence visits.
translations.idiomatic: He held that they should not wait for each other: on the day the Central Army donned felicitations mourning garb, Wenxi need only offer condolences and should not receive condolence visits.

sentences.zh: 至聞喜變除，昆弟亦宜相就寫情，不對客」。

translations.literal: When Wenxi removes mourning, brothers also ought to visit one another to pour out their feelings, and not receive guests."
translations.idiomatic: When Wenxi has concluded his mourning period, the brothers ought likewise to visit one another and give vent to their feelings, but should not receive guests."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: They followed it.
translations.idiomatic: The court accepted his proposal.

sentences.zh: 武帝即位，封竟陵郡王、南徐州刺史，加都督。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu took the throne, he was enfeoffed as Prince of Jingling Commandery, Inspector of South Xuzhou, with the additional title of area commander.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu took the throne, Ziliang was enfeoffed as Prince of Jingling and appointed Inspector of South Xuzhou, with the additional title of area commander.

sentences.zh: 永明二年，為護軍將軍，兼司徒。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongming, he served as General Who Guards the Army, concurrently holding the post of Minister over the Masses.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yongming (484), he was made General Who Guards the Army while also serving as Minister over the Masses.

sentences.zh: 四年，進號車騎將軍。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, he was promoted to the title General of Chariots and Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year (486), he was promoted to General of Chariots and Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 子良少有清尚，禮才好士，居不疑之地，傾意賓客，天下才學皆遊集焉。

translations.literal: Ziliang from youth had pure lofty aims, honored talent and loved scholars, occupied a position free from doubt, poured his heart into guests, and men of talent and learning throughout the realm all gathered there.
translations.idiomatic: Ziliang was from youth high-minded and refined. He honored talent and welcomed scholars. Secure in his position as the emperor's son, he lavished attention on his guests, and men of talent and learning from across the realm flocked to him.

sentences.zh: 善立勝事，夏月客至，為設瓜飲及甘果，著之文教。

translations.literal: He was skilled at setting up excellent events; when guests came in summer he provided melon drinks and sweet fruits, and had them compose essays on civilizing instruction.
translations.idiomatic: He had a gift for arranging splendid gatherings. When guests arrived in summer, he served melon drinks and fine fruits and had them write essays on culture and education.

sentences.zh: 士子文章及朝貴辭翰，皆發教撰錄。

translations.literal: Essays by scholar-gentlemen and compositions by court nobles were all issued on his instruction to be compiled and recorded.
translations.idiomatic: At his direction, scholarly essays and compositions by court dignitaries were all collected and compiled.

sentences.zh: 是時上新視政，水旱不時，子良密啟請原除逋租。

translations.literal: At this time the emperor had newly taken charge of government, floods and droughts came untimely, and Ziliang secretly memorialized asking to remit arrears in rent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had only recently assumed direct rule, and floods and droughts struck in succession. Ziliang submitted a confidential memorial asking that overdue rents be remitted.

sentences.zh: 又陳寬刑息役，輕賦省徭。

translations.literal: He also stated widening punishments and ceasing corvée, lightening levies and reducing labor services.
translations.idiomatic: He also urged lighter punishments, a halt to forced labor, reduced taxes, and relief from corvée duties.

sentences.zh: 並陳「泉鑄歲遠，類多翦鑿，江東大錢，十不一在，公家所受，必須輪郭完全，遂買本一千，加子七百，求請無地，捶革相繼。

translations.literal: He also stated: "Coin minting has gone on for many years; most coins have been clipped and shaved. Of the large coins of Jiangdong, not one in ten remains usable. What the public treasury accepts must have their rims intact and complete, so one buys the base coin for one thousand and adds seven hundred for a subsidiary coin, with no place to plead; beating and distress follow in succession.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote: "Coin has been minted for so many years that most of it has been clipped and filed down. Of the large coins circulating in the Jiangdong region, scarcely one in ten is still intact. Yet what the government will accept must have its rim whole and complete—so a man must buy a full-weight coin for one thousand cash and then pay seven hundred more for a subsidiary coin. There is nowhere to turn for redress, and beatings and confiscations follow one after another.

sentences.zh: 尋完者為用，既不兼兩，回復遷貿，會非委積，徒令小人每嬰困苦。

translations.literal: Soon only intact ones are used; since they cannot serve for both, they are again exchanged and traded; it does not accumulate as stores, but only makes common people repeatedly suffer hardship.
translations.idiomatic: When intact coins are required, a single payment cannot cover both obligations, so people are forced into repeated exchanges—but no real reserve builds up. All it does is visit hardship upon the common people again and again.

sentences.zh: 且錢布相半，為制永久，或聞長宰須令輸直，進違舊科，退容奸利」。

translations.literal: Moreover coin and cloth are half and half as a permanent regulation; one hears that chief officials require payment in cash alone—in advance this violates the old statute, and in retreat it allows corrupt profit."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the rule that tax be paid half in coin and half in cloth was meant to be permanent. Yet one hears that local magistrates demand payment entirely in cash—a practice that violates statute on the one hand and opens the door to corruption on the other."

sentences.zh: 五年，正位司徒，給班劍二十人，侍中如故。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, he took the regular post of Minister over the Masses, was granted twenty ceremonial guards with swords, and remained Palace Attendant as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year (487), he was formally appointed Minister over the Masses, granted an escort of twenty sword-bearing guards, and retained his post as Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 移居雞籠山西邸，集學士抄五經百家，依皇覽例為四部要略千卷。

translations.literal: He moved to the western residence on Cock Cage Mountain, gathered scholars to copy the Five Classics and the hundred schools, and following the precedent of the Huanglan compiled Essential Summaries in Four Sections in a thousand scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: He moved to his western residence on Cock Cage Mountain, gathered scholars to copy the Five Classics and works of the hundred schools, and modeled on the Imperial Overview to produce Essential Summaries in Four Sections—a thousand scrolls in all.

sentences.zh: 招致名僧，講論佛法，造經唄新聲，道俗之盛，江左未有。

translations.literal: He invited renowned monks, discussed Buddhist doctrine, composed new hymn melodies for sutras; the flourishing of clergy and laity the Jiangzuo region had never seen.
translations.idiomatic: He invited celebrated monks to lecture on Buddhist doctrine and composed new hymn melodies for sutra recitation. The splendor of his religious assemblies, drawing both clergy and laity, was unmatched anywhere in the Jiangzuo region.

sentences.zh: 武帝好射雉，子良啟諫。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu loved shooting pheasants; Ziliang memorialized remonstrating.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu loved hunting pheasants, and Ziliang memorialized to dissuade him.

sentences.zh: 先是左衛殿中將軍邯鄲超上書諫射雉，武帝為止，久之，超竟被誅。

translations.literal: Earlier Left Guard Palace General Handan Chao submitted a memorial remonstrating against pheasant hunting; the emperor stopped on his account, but after a long while Chao was ultimately executed.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Handan Chao, General of the Left Guard in the Palace, had submitted a memorial against pheasant hunting, and the emperor desisted for a time. Eventually, however, Chao was put to death.

sentences.zh: 永明末，上將復射雉，子良復諫，前後所陳，上雖不盡納，而深見寵愛。

translations.literal: Near the end of Yongming the emperor was about to hunt pheasants again; Ziliang again remonstrated. Although the emperor did not fully accept what he stated before and after, he was deeply favored and loved.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Yongming era, when the emperor was about to take up pheasant hunting again, Ziliang remonstrated once more. Though the emperor did not accept everything he urged, Ziliang remained deeply favored.

sentences.zh: 又與文惠太子同好釋氏，甚相友悌。

translations.literal: He also shared with Crown Prince Wenhui a love of Buddhism and they were very friendly and fraternal.
translations.idiomatic: He and Crown Prince Wenhui shared a devotion to Buddhism and were close friends.

sentences.zh: 子良敬信尤篤，數于邸園營齋戒，大集朝臣眾僧，至賦食行水，或躬親其事，世頗以為失宰相體。

translations.literal: Ziliang's reverent faith was especially earnest; several times at his residence and garden he held fasting rites, greatly gathering court ministers and many monks, even distributing food and pouring water—sometimes performing the tasks himself—and the age largely regarded this as unbecoming a chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: Ziliang's Buddhist faith was especially fervent. He frequently held fasting assemblies at his residence and gardens, gathering large numbers of court ministers and monks. He even distributed food and poured water for them himself on occasion, and many at the time felt this was unbecoming in a chief minister.

sentences.zh: 勸人為善，未嘗厭倦，以此終致盛名。

translations.literal: Exhorting people to do good, he never grew weary; by this he ultimately attained great fame.
translations.idiomatic: In urging others toward virtue he never tired, and by this he won lasting renown.

sentences.zh: 八年，給三望車。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, he was granted the three-wheeled lookout carriage.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year (490), he was granted the three-wheeled lookout carriage.

sentences.zh: 九年，都下大水，吳興偏劇，子良開倉振救貧病不能立者，於第北立廨收養，給衣及藥。

translations.literal: In the ninth year the capital suffered great flood; Wuxing was especially severe. Ziliang opened granaries to relieve those poor and ill unable to stand, and north of his mansion established offices to take in and support them, supplying clothing and medicine.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year (491), catastrophic floods struck the capital region, with Wuxing especially hard hit. Ziliang opened his granaries to aid the destitute and infirm who could not support themselves, and north of his mansion he set up relief offices to shelter them, providing clothing and medicine.

sentences.zh: 十年，領尚書令、揚州刺史，本官如故。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he held concurrently Director of the Masters of Writing and Inspector of Yangzhou, his original posts remaining as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year (492), he was additionally appointed Director of the Masters of Writing and Inspector of Yangzhou while retaining his existing titles.

sentences.zh: 尋解尚書令，加中書監。

translations.literal: Soon he was relieved of Director of the Masters of Writing and given the additional post of Director of the Central Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he stepped down as Director of the Masters of Writing and was instead made Director of the Central Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 文惠太子薨，武帝檢行東宮，見太子服御羽儀，多過制度，上大怒，以子良與太子善，不啟聞，頗加嫌責。

translations.literal: Crown Prince Wenhui died; Emperor Wu inspected the Eastern Palace and saw the crown prince's clothing, equipage, and ceremonial regalia mostly exceeded regulations. The emperor was greatly angered; because Ziliang was close to the crown prince and had not reported it, he was much reproached with suspicion.
translations.idiomatic: When Crown Prince Wenhui died, Emperor Wu inspected the Eastern Palace and found that the crown prince's clothing, equipage, and ceremonial insignia far exceeded what regulations allowed. The emperor was furious. Because Ziliang had been close to the crown prince and had failed to report the excess, he came under heavy censure.

sentences.zh: 武帝不豫，詔子良甲仗入延昌殿侍醫藥。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu was unwell; he ordered Ziliang with armor and weapons to enter Yanchang Hall to attend medicines.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu fell ill, he ordered Ziliang, with an armed escort, into Yanchang Hall to attend to his medical care.

sentences.zh: 子良啟進沙門於殿戶前誦經，武帝為感夢見優曇缽花。

translations.literal: Ziliang memorialized bringing in monks to recite sutras before the hall doors; Emperor Wu was moved and dreamed of udumbara flowers.
translations.idiomatic: Ziliang had Buddhist monks brought in to recite sutras before the hall doors. The emperor was deeply moved and dreamed of udumbara flowers.

sentences.zh: 子良案佛經宣旨，使禦府以銅為花，插御床四角。

translations.literal: Ziliang consulted Buddhist sutras and proclaimed the emperor's intent, ordering the imperial workshop to make flowers of copper and place them at the four corners of the imperial bed.
translations.idiomatic: Citing Buddhist scripture, Ziliang proclaimed the imperial wish and had the imperial workshops cast copper flowers to place at the four corners of the emperor's bed.

sentences.zh: 日夜在殿內，太孫間日入參。

translations.literal: Day and night he was inside the hall; the imperial grandson entered to attend every other day.
translations.idiomatic: Ziliang remained in the hall day and night, while the imperial grandson came in to attend every other day.

sentences.zh: 武帝暴漸，內外惶懼，百僚皆已變服，物議疑立子良。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu suddenly worsened; inside and outside were fearful and alarmed; all officials had already changed garments; public discussion doubted installing Ziliang.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's condition suddenly worsened. Panic spread inside and outside the palace, and all the officials had already changed into mourning garb. Public opinion turned to the possibility of installing Ziliang as emperor.

sentences.zh: 俄頃而蘇，問太孫所在，因召東宮器甲皆入，遺詔使子良輔政，明帝知尚書事。

translations.literal: In a moment he revived, asked where the imperial grandson was, then summoned all the Eastern Palace arms and armor to enter; the death testament ordered Ziliang to assist government and Emperor Ming to oversee Masters of Writing affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In a moment he revived and asked where the imperial grandson was. He then summoned all the Eastern Palace's weapons and armor into the palace. His deathbed testament named Ziliang to assist in governing and Xiao Luan to manage the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 子良素仁厚，不樂時務，乃推明帝。

translations.literal: Ziliang was by nature benevolent and generous, did not delight in current affairs, and so pushed forward Emperor Ming.
translations.idiomatic: Ziliang was by nature gentle and generous and had no taste for the rough work of politics, so he deferred to Xiao Luan.

sentences.zh: 詔云：「事無大小，悉與鸞參懷」，子良所志也。

translations.literal: The testament stated: "In affairs great and small, deliberate wholly with Luan"—this was Ziliang's wish.
translations.idiomatic: The testament read, "In affairs great and small, consult Luan in full"—and that was exactly what Ziliang wanted.

sentences.zh: 太孫少養于子良妃袁氏，甚著慈愛，既懼前不得立，自此深忌子良。

translations.literal: The imperial grandson was raised from youth by Ziliang's consort Lady Yuan and bore marked affection; fearing he would not be established before, from this he deeply resented Ziliang.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial grandson had been raised from childhood by Ziliang's consort, Lady Yuan, and Ziliang had shown him great affection. Fearing that Ziliang had once stood between him and the throne, from this point on he deeply resented him.

sentences.zh: 大行出太極殿，子良居中書省，帝使虎賁中郎將潘敞二百人仗，屯太極西階之下。

translations.literal: When the imperial funeral procession left Taiji Hall, Ziliang was at the Central Secretariat; the emperor sent Tiger Guard Palace General Pan Chang with two hundred armed men stationed below the western steps of Taiji.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial funeral cortège left Taiji Hall, Ziliang was at the Central Secretariat. The new emperor sent Pan Chang, General of the Tiger Guard in the Palace, with two hundred armed men to encamp at the foot of the western steps of Taiji Hall.

sentences.zh: 成服後，諸王皆出，子良乞停至山陵，不許。

translations.literal: After completion of mourning garments all princes went out; Ziliang begged to remain until the imperial tomb, but was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: After the mourning rites were completed, all the princes were sent away. Ziliang asked to remain until the imperial burial, but permission was denied.

sentences.zh: 進位太傅，增班劍為三十人，本官如故，解侍中。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Grand Tutor, his ceremonial guards increased to thirty men, his original posts as before, and he was relieved of Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Grand Tutor, his sword-bearing escort increased to thirty men, and his other titles were unchanged—but he was stripped of the post of Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 隆昌元年，加殊禮，劍履上殿，入朝不趨，贊拜不名，進督南徐州。

translations.literal: In the first year of Longchang special honors were added: sword and shoes in the hall, no quickening steps entering court, no naming when praised in obeisance; he was advanced to supervise South Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Longchang (494), he was granted special honors: permission to enter the hall wearing sword and shoes, to walk without hurrying at court audiences, and to be hailed in obeisance without having his name spoken. He was also made supervisor of South Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 其年疾篤，謂左右曰：「門外應有異。

translations.literal: That year his illness was severe; he told those beside him: "Outside the gate there ought to be something strange.
translations.idiomatic: That year his illness grew grave. He told those around him, "There ought to be something strange outside the gate.

sentences.zh: 」遣人視，見淮中魚無算，皆浮出水上向城門。

translations.literal: " He sent men to look and saw fish in the Huai beyond counting, all floating on the water facing the city gate.
translations.idiomatic: " He sent someone to look and saw countless fish in the Huai River, all floating on the surface and facing toward the city gate.

sentences.zh: 尋薨，年三十五。

translations.literal: Soon he died, age thirty-five.
translations.idiomatic: He soon died, at the age of thirty-five.

sentences.zh: 所著內外文筆數十卷，雖無文采，多是勸戒。

translations.literal: His literary compositions inside and outside number several tens of scrolls; although without literary elegance, most are exhortations and admonitions.
translations.idiomatic: His collected writings, civil and official, ran to several dozen scrolls. They lacked literary polish for the most part, but most were devoted to exhortation and moral counsel.

sentences.zh: 子良既亡，故人皆來奔赴，陸惠曉于邸門逢袁彖，問之曰：「近者云云，定復何謂？

translations.literal: After Ziliang had died, old friends all came to attend the funeral; Lu Huixiao at the residence gate met Yuan Tan and asked him: "The recent talk—what does it really mean?
translations.idiomatic: After Ziliang's death, his old friends came from far and wide to attend his funeral. At the gate of the residence Lu Huixiao encountered Yuan Tan and asked him, "All this recent talk—what does it really mean?

sentences.zh: 王融見殺，而魏准破膽。

translations.literal: Wang Rong was killed, yet Wei Zhun's gall broke.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Rong has been executed, yet Wei Zhun lost his nerve.

sentences.zh: 道路籍籍，又云竟陵不永天年，有之乎？

translations.literal: The roads are noisy with talk, and they also say Jingling did not enjoy his allotted years—is there truth to it?
translations.idiomatic: The roads are buzzing with rumor, and some say Jingling did not live out his natural span—is there any truth to that?

sentences.zh: 」答曰：「齊氏微弱，已數年矣，爪牙柱石之臣都盡，命之所餘，政風流名士耳。

translations.literal: " He replied: "The Qi house has been weak for several years already; fang and pillar ministers are all gone; what fate leaves is only elegant literary gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: " Yuan Tan replied, "The Qi house has been weakening for years. Its claw-and-fang ministers and pillar statesmen are all gone. What fate leaves alive are only men of letters and reputation.

sentences.zh: 若不立長君，無以鎮安四海。

translations.literal: If one does not establish an elder lord, there is no means to pacify and secure the four seas.
translations.idiomatic: If the court does not enthron a mature ruler, there is no way to secure the realm.

sentences.zh: 王融雖為身計，實安社稷，恨其不能斷事，以至於此。

translations.literal: Although Wang Rong acted for his own sake, he truly secured the altars of soil and grain; the regret is that he could not decide affairs resolutely, leading to this.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Rong may have acted partly for himself, but he truly sought to stabilize the state. The pity is that he lacked the ruthlessness to see it through—and that is how things came to this.

sentences.zh: 道路之談，自為虛說耳，蒼生方塗炭矣，政當瀝耳聽之。

translations.literal: Talk on the roads is itself empty rumor; the common people are just being trampled in fire and charcoal—one ought simply to strain one's ears and listen.
translations.idiomatic: Street talk is idle rumor. The people are being ground to ruin—one should simply listen hard for what matters."

sentences.zh: 」建武中，故吏範雲上表為子良立碑，事不行。

translations.literal: " During Jianwu, a former subordinate Fan Yun submitted a memorial to erect a stele for Ziliang; the matter did not go through.
translations.idiomatic: " During the Jianwu era, Fan Yun, a former subordinate of Ziliang's, submitted a memorial requesting a commemorative stele; the request was denied.

sentences.zh: 子昭胄嗣。

translations.literal: His son Zhaogou succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhaogou succeeded to the title.

sentences.zh: 昭胄字景胤，泛涉書史，有父風，位太常。

translations.literal: Zhaogou's style name was Jingyin; he broadly touched books and histories, had his father's manner, and reached the post of Grand Minister of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaogou, style name Jingyin, was widely read in history and the classics. He inherited his father's character and rose to the post of Grand Minister of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 以封境邊魏，永元元年，改封巴陵王。

translations.literal: Because his fief bordered Wei, in the first year of Yongyuan he was re-enfeoffed as Prince of Baling.
translations.idiomatic: Because his domain bordered Northern Wei, in the first year of Yongyuan (499) he was re-enfeoffed as Prince of Baling.

sentences.zh: 先是，王敬則事起，南康侯子恪在吳郡，明帝慮有同異，召諸王侯入宮，晉安王寶義及江陵公寶覽住中書省，高、武諸孫住西省，敕人各兩左右自隨，過此依軍法；

translations.literal: Earlier, when Wang Jingze's affair arose, Marquis of Nankang Zike was in Wu Commandery; Emperor Ming feared disaffection and summoned all princes and marquises into the palace; Prince of Jin'an BaoYi and Duke of Jiangling BaoLan lodged in the Central Secretariat; the grandsons of Gao and Wu lodged in the Western Secretariat; he ordered each person to have two attendants follow—beyond this military law applied;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Wang Jingze's revolt broke out, Zike, Marquis of Nankang, was in Wu Commandery. Fearing disloyalty among the princes, Emperor Ming summoned all the kings and marquises into the palace. Prince Bao Yi of Jin'an and Duke Bao Lan of Jiangling were quartered in the Central Secretariat; the grandsons of Emperors Gao and Wu were quartered in the Western Secretariat. Each was allowed only two personal attendants—anyone exceeding that limit was subject to martial law.

sentences.zh: 孩抱者乳母隨入。

translations.literal: Those held in arms had wet nurses follow in.
translations.idiomatic: Infants in arms were permitted a wet nurse to accompany them inside.

sentences.zh: 其夜並將加害，賴子恪至乃免。

translations.literal: That night they were all about to be killed; thanks to Zike's arrival they were spared.
translations.idiomatic: That very night they were all to be executed—but when Zike arrived, they were spared.

sentences.zh: 自建武以來，高、武王侯，居常震怖，朝不保夕，至是尤甚。

translations.literal: From Jianwu onward the princes and marquises of Gao and Wu had constantly lived in terror, not sure of surviving the day, and at this time it was especially severe.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Jianwu era, the princes and marquises descended from Emperors Gao and Wu had lived in constant terror, never sure they would survive to the next day—and now their dread was worse than ever.

sentences.zh: 及陳顯達起事，王侯復入宮，昭胄懲往時之懼，與弟永新侯昭穎逃奔江西，變形為道人。

translations.literal: When Chen Xianda raised troops, the princes again entered the palace; Zhaogou, mindful of past fear, with his younger brother Yongxin Marquis Zhaoying fled west of the river, changing form to become Daoist priests.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Xianda rose in rebellion, the princes were once again confined in the palace. Mindful of what had happened before, Zhaogou fled with his younger brother Zhaoying, Marquis of Yongxin, west of the Yangzi, disguising themselves as Daoist priests.

sentences.zh: 崔慧景舉兵，昭胄兄弟出投之。

translations.literal: Cui Huijing raised troops; the Zhaogou brothers went out to join him.
translations.idiomatic: When Cui Huijing took up arms, the Zhaogou brothers went to join him.

sentences.zh: 慧景敗，昭胄兄弟首出投台軍主胡松，各以王侯還第，不自安，謀為身計。

translations.literal: Huijing was defeated; the Zhaogou brothers were first to go out and surrender to platform army commander Hu Song; each returned to his mansion as prince and marquis, did not feel secure, and plotted for their own sake.
translations.idiomatic: When Huijing was defeated, the Zhaogou brothers were the first to surrender to Hu Song, commander of the capital army. They returned to their mansions with their titles intact but felt no security and began plotting for their own survival.

sentences.zh: 子良故防合桑偃為梅蟲兒軍副，結前巴西太守蕭寅，謀立昭胄。

translations.literal: Ziliang's former guard commander Sang Yan served as deputy to Mei Chong'er's army; he joined with former Administrator of Baxi Xiao Yin, plotting to establish Zhaogou.
translations.idiomatic: Sang Yan, Ziliang's former household guard commander and now deputy to Mei Chong'er's forces, joined with Xiao Yin, former Administrator of Baxi, in a plot to install Zhaogou on the throne.

sentences.zh: 昭胄許事克用寅為尚書左僕射、護軍，以寅有部曲，大事皆委之。

translations.literal: Zhaogou promised if the affair succeeded to use Yin as Left Vice Director of the Secretariat and General Who Guards the Army; because Yin had personal troops, all great affairs were entrusted to him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaogou promised that if the plot succeeded, Yin would be made Left Vice Director of the Secretariat and General Who Guards the Army. Because Yin commanded private troops, Zhaogou delegated all major decisions to him.

sentences.zh: 時胡松領軍在新亭，寅遣人說之，松許諾。

translations.literal: At this time Hu Song commanded the army at Xinting; Yin sent men to persuade him and Song agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Song was then commanding troops at Xinting. Yin sent envoys to win him over, and Hu Song agreed to join.

sentences.zh: 又張欣泰嘗為雍州，亦有部曲，昭胄又遣房天寶以謀告之，欣泰聞命回應。

translations.literal: Moreover Zhang Xintai had once been in Yongzhou and also had personal troops; Zhaogou again sent Fang Tianbao to inform him of the plot, and Xintai upon hearing the order replied in agreement.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xintai, who had once governed Yongzhou and also commanded private troops, was likewise approached when Zhaogou sent Fang Tianbao to disclose the plot. Xintai agreed on the spot.

sentences.zh: 蕭寅左右華永達知其謀，以告禦刀朱光尚。

translations.literal: Xiao Yin's attendant Hua Yongda knew their plot and reported it to Imperial Guardsman Zhu Guangshang.
translations.idiomatic: Hua Yongda, a member of Xiao Yin's staff, learned of the conspiracy and reported it to Zhu Guangshang, an imperial guard.

sentences.zh: 光尚挾左道以惑東昏，因謂東昏曰：「昨見蔣王，雲巴陵王在外結黨欲反，須官出行，仍從萬春門入，事不可量。

translations.literal: Guangshang relied on heterodox arts to delude Emperor Donghun, then said to Donghun: "Yesterday I saw Prince Jiang, who said the Prince of Baling is outside forming a faction wishing to rebel; when the ruler goes out, they will enter from Wanchun Gate—the affair cannot be measured.
translations.idiomatic: Guangshang, who practiced sorcery, used the occult to sway Emperor Donghun. He told him, "Yesterday I saw Prince Jiang, who said the Prince of Baling is out there building a faction and planning rebellion. When Your Majesty goes out, they mean to enter through Wanchun Gate—the consequences are hard to foresee.

sentences.zh: 」時東昏日游走，聞此說大懼，不復出四十餘日。

translations.literal: " At that time Donghun daily roamed about; hearing this explanation he was greatly afraid and did not go out again for more than forty days.
translations.idiomatic: " Donghun had been roaming about every day. When he heard this, he was terrified and did not leave the palace again for more than forty days.

sentences.zh: 偃等議募健兒百餘人，從萬春門入，突取之。

translations.literal: Yan and the others planned to recruit more than a hundred stalwart youths to enter from Wanchun Gate and seize him by surprise.
translations.idiomatic: Yan and his co-conspirators proposed recruiting more than a hundred strong fighters to enter through Wanchun Gate and seize the emperor by force.

sentences.zh: 昭胄以為不可。

translations.literal: Zhaogou thought it impossible.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaogou objected that this was unwise.

sentences.zh: 偃同黨王山沙慮事久無成，以事告禦刀徐僧重，寅遣人殺山沙于路。

translations.literal: Yan's fellow Wang Shansha, fearing the affair long without success, reported the matter to Imperial Guardsman Xu Sengzhong; Yin sent men to kill Shansha on the road.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shansha, a co-conspirator of Yan's, grew anxious as the plot dragged on without success and reported it to Xu Sengzhong, an imperial guard. Yin sent men to kill Shansha on the road.

sentences.zh: 吏於麝幐中得其事蹟，昭胄兄弟與同黨皆伏誅。

translations.literal: Officials found the records of the affair in a musk pouch; the Zhaogou brothers and fellow conspirators all suffered execution.
translations.idiomatic: Officials discovered documentary evidence of the plot in a musk pouch. Zhaogou, his brother, and their co-conspirators were all executed.

sentences.zh: 梁受禪，降封昭胄子同為監利侯。

translations.literal: When Liang received the abdication, Zhaogou's son Tong was demoted and enfeoffed as Marquis of Jianli.
translations.idiomatic: When the Liang dynasty succeeded to the mandate, Zhaogou's son Tong was demoted to Marquis of Jianli.

sentences.zh: 同弟賁字文奐，形不滿六尺，神識耿介。

translations.literal: Tong's younger brother Ben's style name was Wenhuan; his form did not reach six chi, his spirit and understanding were upright and uncompromising.
translations.idiomatic: Tong's younger brother Ben, style name Wenhuan, stood less than six feet tall, but his mind was sharp and uncompromising.

sentences.zh: 幼好學，有文才，能書善畫，於扇上圖山水，咫尺之內，便覺萬里為遙。

translations.literal: From youth he loved learning, had literary talent, could write and was skilled at painting; on a fan he depicted landscapes—in within a foot one felt ten thousand li were distant.
translations.idiomatic: From childhood he loved learning and had literary gifts. He was accomplished in calligraphy and painting; when he painted landscapes on a fan, the tiny surface seemed to open onto vistas a thousand miles away.

sentences.zh: 矜慎不傳，自娛而已。

translations.literal: Self-restrained and cautious, he did not pass works on—only for his own amusement.
translations.idiomatic: Reserved and careful, he would not let his work circulate; he created only for his own pleasure.

sentences.zh: 好著述，嘗著西京雜記六十卷。

translations.literal: He loved composing; he once authored Western Capital Miscellaneous Records in sixty scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: He loved to write and once composed Western Capital Miscellany in sixty scrolls.

sentences.zh: 起家湘東王法曹參軍，得一府歡心。

translations.literal: He first served as Legal Bureau Aide on the staff of the Prince of Xiangdong, winning the whole staff's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: He began his career as Legal Bureau Aide on the staff of the Prince of Xiangdong and won the affection of the entire household.

sentences.zh: 及亂，王為檄，賁讀至「偃師南望，無復儲胥露寒，河陽北臨，或有穹廬氈帳」，乃曰：「聖制此句，非為過似，如體目朝廷，非關序賊。

translations.literal: When disorder arose the prince drafted a proclamation; Ben reading to "Yanshi looks south—no more storehouses or exposed sentinels in the cold; Heyang faces north—or perhaps yurt tents of felt" then said: "The sage composed this line not because the simile is excessive—it is as though describing the court, unrelated to arranging against the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: When rebellion broke out, the prince drafted a military proclamation. Ben read as far as the line, "From Yanshi looking south, no storied towers stand in the cold; from Heyang facing north, one might find nomad tents of felt," and remarked, "In composing this line, Your Highness was not guilty of excessive simile—it reads as though you were describing the imperial court itself, not the enemy.

sentences.zh: 」王聞之大怒，收付獄，遂以餓終。

translations.literal: " The prince hearing was greatly angered, seized him and sent to prison, and he ultimately ended by starvation.
translations.idiomatic: " The prince was furious, had him arrested and imprisoned, and Ben eventually starved to death.

sentences.zh: 又追戮賁屍，乃著懷舊傳以謗之，極言誣毀。

translations.literal: Moreover he pursued posthumous execution of Ben's corpse, then authored Nostalgic Biographies to slander him, speaking to the utmost of false accusation and vilification.
translations.idiomatic: The prince even had Ben's corpse mutilated in a posthumous execution and then wrote Nostalgic Biographies to defame him, reviling him in the harshest terms.

sentences.zh: 廬陵王子卿字雲長，武帝第三子也。

translations.literal: Xiao Ziqing, Prince of Luling, style name Yunchang, was Emperor Wu's third son.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Ziqing, Prince of Luling—style name Yunchang—was Emperor Wu's third son.

sentences.zh: 建元元年，封臨汝縣公。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jianyuan he was enfeoffed as Duke of Linru County.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jianyuan (479), he was enfeoffed as Duke of Linru.

sentences.zh: 武帝即位，為郢州刺史，加都督。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu took the throne he was made Inspector of Yingzhou, with the additional title of area commander.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu took the throne, Ziqing was made Inspector of Yingzhou, with the additional title of area commander.

sentences.zh: 子卿諸子中無德，又與魚復侯子響同生，故無寵。

translations.literal: Among all the emperor's sons Ziqing lacked virtue, and he was born of the same mother as Marquis of Yufu Zixiang, therefore he received no favor.
translations.idiomatic: Among the emperor's sons Ziqing stood out for his lack of virtue, and because he shared a mother with Zixiang, Marquis of Yufu, he won no favor at court.

sentences.zh: 徙都督、荊州刺史。

translations.literal: He was transferred as area commander and Inspector of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned as area commander and Inspector of Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 始興王為益州，子卿解督。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Shixing took Yizhou, Ziqing was relieved of the area command.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Shixing was posted to Yizhou, Ziqing was relieved of his area command.

sentences.zh: 子卿在鎮，營造服飾，多違制度，作玳瑁乘具。

translations.literal: Ziqing at his post constructed clothing and adornments mostly violating regulations, making tortoiseshell riding equipage.
translations.idiomatic: While posted to his province, Ziqing had clothing and ornaments made in violation of regulations, including riding gear fashioned from tortoiseshell.

sentences.zh: 詔責之，令速送都；

translations.literal: An edict reproached him and ordered them sent speedily to the capital;
translations.idiomatic: An edict censured him and ordered the items sent to the capital at once;

sentences.zh: 又作銀鐙、金薄裹箭腳，亦便速壞去。

translations.literal: Also he made silver stirrups and arrow shafts wrapped in gold foil—he was likewise to destroy them speedily.
translations.idiomatic: He had also made silver stirrups and arrow shafts wrapped in gold foil—these too were to be destroyed immediately.

sentences.zh: 凡諸服章，自今不啟專輒作者，當得痛杖。

translations.literal: For all such garments and insignia, from now on whoever without reporting acts on his own authority shall receive severe beating.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth, anyone who produced such regalia on his own authority without imperial approval would receive a severe beating.

sentences.zh: 又曰：「汝比令讀學，今年轉成長，學既勿就，得敕如風過耳，使吾失氣。」

translations.literal: It also said: "You were recently ordered to study; this year you grow more mature—yet learning has not been achieved; receiving edicts is like wind passing the ear, making me lose breath."
translations.idiomatic: The edict also read, "I ordered you to apply yourself to your studies. You are grown now, yet you have accomplished nothing. My commands pass through you like wind through the ears—and you have taken the wind out of me."

sentences.zh: 永明十年，為都督、南豫州刺史。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Yongming he served as area commander and Inspector of South Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Yongming (492), he was made area commander and Inspector of South Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 之鎮，道中戲部伍為水軍，上聞大怒，殺其典簽。

translations.literal: Going to his post, on the road he playfully arranged his retinue as a naval force; when the emperor heard he was greatly angered and killed his chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: On his way to his post, he amused himself by drilling his retinue as a naval force. When the emperor heard of it he was furious and had Ziqing's chief clerk executed.

sentences.zh: 遣宜都王鏗代之。

translations.literal: He sent Prince of Yidu Keng to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Prince Keng of Yidu to replace him.

sentences.zh: 子卿還第，至崩不與相見。

translations.literal: Ziqing returned to his mansion; until the emperor's death he was not granted an audience.
translations.idiomatic: Ziqing returned to his mansion and was never granted another audience before the emperor died.

sentences.zh: 魚復侯子響字雲音，武帝第四子也。

translations.literal: Xiao Zixiang, Marquis of Yufu, style name Yun Yin, was Emperor Wu's fourth son.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Zixiang, Marquis of Yufu—style name Yun Yin—was Emperor Wu's fourth son.

sentences.zh: 豫章王嶷無子，養子響。

translations.literal: Prince of Yuzhang Niao had no son and adopted Zixiang.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Niao of Yuzhang had no sons and adopted Zixiang.

sentences.zh: 後嶷有子，表留為嫡。

translations.literal: Later Niao had a son; he memorialized to retain Zixiang as legitimate heir.
translations.idiomatic: When Niao later had a son of his own, he petitioned to keep Zixiang as his legitimate heir.

sentences.zh: 武帝即位，為南彭城、臨淮二郡太守。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu took the throne, [Zixiang] became Grand Administrator of the two commanderies of Nan Pengcheng and Linhuai.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu acceded to the throne, Zixiang was appointed Grand Administrator of the two commanderies of Nan Pengcheng and Linhuai.

sentences.zh: 子響勇力絕人，開弓四斛力，數在園池中帖騎馳走竹樹下，身無虧傷。

translations.literal: Zixiang's courage and strength surpassed other men; he could draw a bow of four hu strength; many times in garden ponds he rode close mounted, galloping beneath bamboo trees, his body without injury.
translations.idiomatic: Zixiang's strength and daring were unmatched. He could draw a bow rated at four hu, and would often ride at full gallop with his body nearly touching the saddle beneath the bamboo groves in the palace gardens, never suffering so much as a scratch.

sentences.zh: 既出繼，車服異諸王，每入朝輒忿，拳打車壁，武帝知之，令車服與皇子同。

translations.literal: Once he left the succession, his carriage and robes differed from other princes; each time he entered court he grew angry and punched the carriage walls. Emperor Wu learned of this and ordered his carriage and robes made the same as the imperial princes'.
translations.idiomatic: Once he had been given in adoption, his carriage and insignia differed from those of the other princes. Every time he came to court he would fly into a rage and punch the sides of his carriage.
