When Emperor Wu learned of this, he ordered that Zixiang's carriage and robes be made identical to those of the imperial princes.

sentences.zh: 永明六年，有司奏子響宜還本，乃封巴東郡王。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Yongming, the relevant offices memorialized that Zixiang ought to return to his original [clan], and he was enfeoffed as King of Badong Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Yongming, the relevant offices memorialized that Zixiang should return to his birth family, whereupon he was enfeoffed as King of Badong.

sentences.zh: 七年，為都督、荊州刺史。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, he became Area Commander and Inspector of Jing Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, he was appointed Area Commander and Inspector of Jing Province.

sentences.zh: 直合將軍董蠻粗有氣力，子響要與同行。

translations.literal: Direct Attendant General Dong Man was somewhat strong; Zixiang invited him to travel together.
translations.idiomatic: Direct Attendant General Dong Man was a man of some physical strength, and Zixiang asked him to accompany him on the journey.

sentences.zh: 蠻曰：「殿下癲如雷，敢相隨邪？

translations.literal: Man said: "Your Highness is mad as thunder—dare one follow along?
translations.idiomatic: Man said, "Your Highness is fierce as thunder itself—how dare anyone follow you?

sentences.zh: 」子響笑曰：「君敢出此語，亦復奇癲。

translations.literal: " Zixiang laughed and said: "You dare speak such words—you too are strangely mad.
translations.idiomatic: " Zixiang laughed and said, "You dare say such a thing—you're strangely wild yourself.

sentences.zh: 」上聞而不悅，曰：「人名蠻，復何容得蘊藉。

translations.literal: " The emperor heard and was displeased, saying: "When a man's name is Man [Barbarian], how can he be allowed refinement?
translations.idiomatic: " When the emperor heard of this he was displeased and said, "A man named Barbarian—how is he supposed to carry himself with refinement?

sentences.zh: 」乃改名為仲舒。

translations.literal: " [Zixiang] then renamed him Zhongshu.
translations.idiomatic: " Zixiang thereupon renamed him Zhongshu.

sentences.zh: 謂曰：「今日仲舒，何如昔日仲舒？

translations.literal: He said to him: "Today's Zhongshu—how does he compare with yesterday's Zhongshu?
translations.idiomatic: He asked him, "How does today's Zhongshu compare with yesterday's Zhongshu?

sentences.zh: 」答曰：「昔日仲舒，出自私庭，今日仲舒，降自天帝，以此言之，勝昔遠矣。

translations.literal: " He answered: "Yesterday's Zhongshu came from a private household; today's Zhongshu descended from the Heavenly Emperor—speaking thus, he far surpasses the former.
translations.idiomatic: " He answered, "Yesterday's Zhongshu came from a private household; today's Zhongshu was sent down by the Son of Heaven. By that measure, he far surpasses his former self.

sentences.zh: 」上稱善。

translations.literal: " The emperor praised it as good.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor commended the reply.

sentences.zh: 子響少好武，帶仗左右六十人，皆有膽幹，數在內齋殺牛置酒，與之聚樂。

translations.literal: Zixiang from youth loved martial affairs; he kept armed attendants of sixty men, all possessing courage and ability; many times in the inner fasting hall he killed oxen and set out wine, gathering merriment with them.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Zixiang loved martial pursuits. He kept sixty armed attendants about him, all men of courage and capability, and would often slaughter oxen and set out wine in the inner hall, feasting and making merry with them.

sentences.zh: 令私作錦袍絳襖，欲餉蠻交易器仗。

translations.literal: He ordered privately made brocade robes and crimson padded jackets, intending to offer Man in exchange for weapons and armor.
translations.idiomatic: He had brocade robes and crimson padded jackets made in secret, intending to offer them to Man in exchange for weapons and armor.

sentences.zh: 長史劉寅等連名密啟，上敕精檢，寅等懼，欲秘之。

translations.literal: Chief Administrator Liu Yin and others jointly signed a secret memorial; the emperor ordered a thorough investigation; Yin and the others were afraid and wished to conceal it.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Administrator Liu Yin and others jointly submitted a confidential memorial. The emperor ordered a thorough investigation, and Yin and his colleagues, frightened, wished to keep the matter secret.

sentences.zh: 子響聞台使至，不見敕，乃召寅及司馬席恭穆、諮議參軍江悆、殷曇粲、中兵參軍周彥、典簽吳修之、王賢宗、魏景深等俱入，於琴台下並斬之。

translations.literal: Zixiang heard that capital envoys had arrived but saw no edict; he then summoned Yin and Staff Supervisor Xi Gongmu, Advisory Aide Jiang Yu, Yin Tancai, Central Army Aide Zhou Yan, chief clerks Wu Xiuzhi, Wang Xianzong, Wei Jingshen, and others all to enter, and below the Qin Terrace beheaded them all together.
translations.idiomatic: When Zixiang heard that envoys from the capital had arrived yet saw no edict, he summoned Yin together with Staff Supervisor Xi Gongmu, Advisory Aide Jiang Yu, Yin Tancai, Central Army Aide Zhou Yan, and chief clerks Wu Xiuzhi, Wang Xianzong, and Wei Jingshen, and had them all beheaded beneath the Qin Terrace.

sentences.zh: 上聞之怒，遣衛尉胡諧之、遊擊將軍尹略、中書舍人茹法亮領羽林三千人檢捕群小。

translations.literal: The emperor heard and was enraged; he sent Commandant of the Guard Hu Xiezhi, Mobile General Yin Lve, and Palace Secretary Ru Faliang leading three thousand Feathered Forest guards to investigate and capture the lesser followers.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard of this he flew into a rage and dispatched Commandant of the Guard Hu Xiezhi, Mobile General Yin Lve, and Palace Secretary Ru Faliang at the head of three thousand Feathered Forest guards to investigate and arrest Zixiang's followers.

sentences.zh: 敕「子響若束手自歸，可全其性命」。

translations.literal: An edict [said]: "If Zixiang binds himself and returns of his own accord, his life may be spared."
translations.idiomatic: An edict declared, "If Zixiang surrenders with bound hands of his own accord, his life will be spared."

sentences.zh: 諧之等至江津，築城燕尾洲。

translations.literal: Xiezhi and the others reached the Jiang Ford and built a fort on Swallowtail Islet.
translations.idiomatic: Xiezhi and his men reached the Jiang Ford and constructed a fort on Swallowtail Islet.

sentences.zh: 子響白服登城，頻遣信與相聞，曰：「天下豈有兒反，身不作賊，直是粗疏。

translations.literal: Zixiang in white garments ascended the wall, repeatedly sending messengers to communicate, saying: "Under Heaven can there be a son who rebels? I myself am no bandit—it is simply heedlessness.
translations.idiomatic: Clad in white, Zixiang mounted the city wall and sent messenger after messenger to open communications, saying, "Under Heaven, can a son truly be called a rebel? I am no traitor—this is merely heedlessness on my part.

sentences.zh: 今便單舸還闕，何築城見捉邪？

translations.literal: Now I shall at once return alone in a single boat to the capital—why build a fort to seize me?
translations.idiomatic: I mean to return at once to the capital in a single boat—why build a fort just to capture me?

sentences.zh: 」尹略獨答曰：「誰將汝反父人共語。

translations.literal: " Yin Lve alone answered: "Who would let you, a man who rebelled against his father, speak with him?
translations.idiomatic: " Yin Lve alone replied, "Who would allow a son who rebelled against his father to negotiate with him?

sentences.zh: 」子響聞之唯灑泣。

translations.literal: " Zixiang heard this and could only shed tears.
translations.idiomatic: " When Zixiang heard this he could only weep.

sentences.zh: 又送牛數十頭，酒二百石，果饌三十輿，略棄之江流。

translations.literal: [Zixiang] also sent several dozen head of cattle, two hundred shi of wine, and thirty cartloads of fruits and delicacies; Lve cast them into the river current.
translations.idiomatic: Zixiang also sent several dozen oxen, two hundred shi of wine, and thirty cartloads of fruit and delicacies; Lve had them cast into the river.

sentences.zh: 子響膽力之士王沖天不勝忿，乃率黨度洲攻壘斬略，而諧之、法亮單艇奔逸。

translations.literal: Zixiang's bold and strong man Wang Chongtian, unable to bear his anger, then led his faction across the islet to attack the fort and kill Lve; Xiezhi and Faliang in single boats fled.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chongtian, one of Zixiang's bravest men, unable to contain his fury, led a band across the islet, stormed the fort, and killed Lve, while Xiezhi and Faliang fled each in a lone boat.

sentences.zh: 上又遣丹陽尹蕭順之領兵繼之，子響即日將白衣左右三十人，乘舴艋中流下都。

translations.literal: The emperor again sent Metropolitan Governor of Danyang Xiao Shunzhi leading troops to follow up; that same day Zixiang took thirty attendants in white garments, boarded small boats, and flowed downstream to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then sent Metropolitan Governor Xiao Shunzhi of Danyang with troops in pursuit. That same day Zixiang took thirty attendants dressed in white, boarded small boats, and sailed downstream toward the capital.

sentences.zh: 初，順之將發，文惠太子素忌子響，密遣不許還，令便為之所。

translations.literal: Initially, when Shunzhi was about to depart, Crown Prince Wenhui had long envied Zixiang; he secretly sent word forbidding his return and ordering that he be dealt with on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: Before Shunzhi set out, Crown Prince Wenhui, who had long resented Zixiang, secretly sent word forbidding his return and instructing Shunzhi to dispose of him then and there.

sentences.zh: 子響及見順之，欲自申明，順之不許，於射堂縊之。

translations.literal: When Zixiang reached and saw Shunzhi, he wished to explain himself; Shunzhi would not permit it and strangled him in the archery hall.
translations.idiomatic: When Zixiang met Shunzhi and tried to plead his case, Shunzhi would not hear him and strangled him in the archery hall.

sentences.zh: 有司奏絕子響屬籍，賜為蛸氏。

translations.literal: The relevant offices memorialized to cut Zixiang from the clan register and bestow upon him the surname Xiao.
translations.idiomatic: The relevant offices memorialized to strike Zixiang from the imperial clan register and bestow upon him the surname of the Xiao clan as punishment.

sentences.zh: 子響密作啟數紙，藏妃王氏裙腰中，具自申明，云：「輕舫還闕不得，此苦之深，唯願矜憐，無使竹帛齊有反父之子，父有害子之名。

translations.literal: Zixiang secretly wrote several sheets of memorial, hiding them in Consort Wang's skirt waist, fully explaining himself, saying: "In a light boat I could not return to court—this suffering runs deep; I only wish compassion, that records not together bear a son who rebelled against his father, nor his father the name of one who harmed his son.
translations.idiomatic: Zixiang secretly wrote several memorials and hid them in the waistband of his consort Lady Wang's skirt, setting forth his full account: "Unable to return to court even in a light boat—the anguish of this is beyond words. I beg only for compassion, that history not record alongside one another both a son who rebelled against his father and a father who destroyed his son.

sentences.zh: 」及順之還，上心甚怪恨。

translations.literal: " When Shunzhi returned, the emperor's heart was greatly astonished and resentful.
translations.idiomatic: " When Shunzhi returned, the emperor was deeply troubled and filled with regret.

sentences.zh: 百日于華林為子響作齋，上自行香，對諸朝士嚬蹙。

translations.literal: On the hundredth day [after death], at Hualin a service was held for Zixiang; the emperor personally burned incense, toward the court gentlemen frowning deeply.
translations.idiomatic: On the hundredth day after his death a memorial service for Zixiang was held at Hualin. The emperor burned incense himself, his face deeply furrowed before the assembled courtiers.

sentences.zh: 及見順之，嗚咽移時，左右莫不掩涕。

translations.literal: When he saw Shunzhi, he sobbed for a long time; those at his side none did not cover their tears.
translations.idiomatic: When he saw Shunzhi he wept aloud for a long while, and none among his attendants could keep from shedding tears.

sentences.zh: 他日出景陽山，見一沐透擲悲鳴，問後堂丞：「此沐何意？

translations.literal: Another day going out to Jingyang Mountain, he saw a macaque cast about wailing mournfully; he asked the Rear Hall Attendant: "What is this macaque's meaning?
translations.idiomatic: On another day, while out at Jingyang Mountain, he saw a macaque casting itself about and crying mournfully. He asked the Rear Hall Attendant, "What is that macaque doing?

sentences.zh: 」答曰：「沐子前日墮崖致死，其母求之不見，故爾。

translations.literal: " He answered: "The macaque's young yesterday fell from a cliff and died; its mother seeks it and cannot find it, hence this.
translations.idiomatic: " He answered, "The macaque's infant fell from the cliff and died yesterday. Its mother searches for it in vain, and so she wails.

sentences.zh: 」上因憶子響，歔欷良久，不自勝。

translations.literal: " The emperor thereupon remembered Zixiang, sighing for a long time, unable to restrain himself.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor was reminded of Zixiang and sighed at length, unable to contain his grief.

sentences.zh: 順之慚懼，感病，遂以憂卒。

translations.literal: Shunzhi ashamed and afraid, contracted illness, and finally died of grief.
translations.idiomatic: Shunzhi, stricken with shame and fear, fell ill and died of grief.

sentences.zh: 於是豫章王嶷上表曰：「故庶人蛸子響識懷靡樹，見淪不逞，肆憤一朝，取陷凶德，身膏草野，未雲塞釁。

translations.literal: Thereupon Prince of Yuzhang Niao submitted a memorial saying: "The former commoner Xiao Zixiang's understanding and intent had no tree to stand upon; seeing himself sunk and unable to advance, in one morning he unleashed rage, fell into evil conduct, his body anointed the wild grass—this does not yet say the offense is expiated.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Prince Niao of Yuzhang submitted a memorial stating, "The late commoner of the Xiao clan, Zixiang, had nowhere to anchor his aspirations. Seeing himself brought low and unable to prevail, he unleashed his fury in a single day and fell into wicked conduct; his body now fertilizes the wild grass, yet this scarcely atones for his crime.

sentences.zh: 但歸罪司戮，迷而知返，撫事惟往，載傷心目。

translations.literal: But returning blame to the executioner's blade, lost yet knowing to return, touching the matter with only the past, it deeply wounds heart and eye.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he accepted the executioner's blade, lost his way but sought to return, and faced the matter with only the past in his heart—a sight that wounds the heart and eye to recall.

sentences.zh: 伏願一下天矜，使得旋窆餘麓，豈伊窮骸被德，實且天下歸仁。

translations.literal: I prostrate and wish Your Majesty once to extend Heaven's compassion, enabling him to be re-interred on a hillside; would that not only his poor bones receive grace, but in truth the realm turn toward benevolence.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly beg Your Majesty to extend Heaven's compassion just once, that he may be reburied on a distant hillside—not only so that his poor remains may receive grace, but so that all under Heaven may turn toward benevolence.

sentences.zh: 」上不許，貶為魚復侯。

translations.literal: " The emperor did not consent; [Zixiang] was demoted to Marquis of Yufu.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor refused. Zixiang's title was reduced to Marquis of Yufu.

sentences.zh: 安陸王子敬字雲端，武帝第五子也。

translations.literal: Prince of Anlu Zijing, style name Yun Duan, was Emperor Wu's fifth son.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Zijing, Prince of Anlu—style name Yun Duan—was Emperor Wu's fifth son.

sentences.zh: 初封應城縣公。

translations.literal: Initially he was enfeoffed as Duke of Yingcheng County.
translations.idiomatic: He was first enfeoffed as Duke of Yingcheng County.

sentences.zh: 先是子敬所生早亡，帝命貴妃范氏母養之，及范氏薨，而子及婦服制，禮無明文。

translations.literal: Previously Zijing's birth mother had died early; the emperor ordered Honored Consort Fan to rear him as mother; when Fan died, [whether] the son and daughter-in-law should observe mourning—the rites had no explicit text.
translations.idiomatic: Zijing's birth mother had died while he was still young, and the emperor had ordered Honored Consort Fan to raise him as his mother. When Fan died, there was no explicit provision in the rites governing whether the son and his wife should observe mourning for her.

sentences.zh: 永明中，尚書令王儉議：「孫為慈孫，婦為慈婦，姑為慈姑，宜制期年服。

translations.literal: Mid-Yongming, Director of the Masters of Writing Wang Jian proposed: "The grandson is a filial grandson, the daughter-in-law a filial daughter-in-law, the mother-in-law a filial mother-in-law—they ought to observe one-year mourning.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yongming era, Director of the Masters of Writing Wang Jian proposed, "The grandson should be a filial grandson, the daughter-in-law a filial daughter-in-law, and the mother-in-law a filial mother-in-law—they ought to observe one year of mourning.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " [The emperor] followed this.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 十年，位散騎常侍、撫軍將軍、丹陽尹。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, his posts were Regular Attendant, General Who Pacifies the Army, and Metropolitan Governor of Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he held the posts of Regular Attendant, General Who Pacifies the Army, and Metropolitan Governor of Danyang.

sentences.zh: 十一年，加車騎將軍。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, he was promoted to General of Chariots and Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he was promoted to General of Chariots and Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 隆昌元年，遷都督、南兗州刺史。

translations.literal: In the first year of Longchang, he was transferred to Area Commander and Inspector of Southern Yan Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Longchang he was transferred to Area Commander and Inspector of Southern Yan Province.

sentences.zh: 延興元年，加侍中。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yanxing, he was promoted to Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yanxing he was promoted to Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 明帝除諸蕃王，遣中護軍王玄邈征九江，王廣之襲殺子敬。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming eliminated the various feudal kings; he sent Central Guard General Wang Xuanyao to campaign against Jiujiang; Wang Guangzhi launched a surprise attack and killed Zijing.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming moved to eliminate the feudal princes, he sent Central Guard General Wang Xuanyao to campaign against Jiujiang, and Wang Guangzhi launched a surprise attack and killed Zijing.

sentences.zh: 初，子敬為武帝所留心，帝不豫，有意立子敬為太子，代太孫。

translations.literal: Initially Zijing was in Emperor Wu's special regard; when the emperor was unwell, he intended to establish Zijing as crown prince, replacing the imperial grandson.
translations.idiomatic: Zijing had long been a favorite of Emperor Wu's. When the emperor fell ill, he considered making Zijing crown prince in place of the imperial grandson.

sentences.zh: 子敬與太孫俱入參畢同出，武帝目送子敬良久，曰：「阿五鈍。

translations.literal: Zijing and the imperial grandson together entered for audience and together departed; Emperor Wu gazed after Zijing for a long time and said, "Ah Fifth is dull.
translations.idiomatic: Zijing and the imperial grandson entered for audience together and left together. Emperor Wu watched Zijing go for a long while and said, "Ah Fifth is slow-witted.

sentences.zh: 」由此代換之意乃息。

translations.literal: " Thereby the intention to replace [the heir] ceased.
translations.idiomatic: " With that, the plan to replace the heir was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 晉安王子懋字雲昌，武帝第七子也。

translations.literal: Prince of Jin'an Zimao, style name Yun Chang, was Emperor Wu's seventh son.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Zimao, Prince of Jin'an—style name Yun Chang—was Emperor Wu's seventh son.

sentences.zh: 諸子中最為清恬，有意思，廉讓好學。

translations.literal: Among all the sons he was the most pure and tranquil, possessed meaningful intent, modest and studious.
translations.idiomatic: Among all the emperor's sons he was the most serene and thoughtful—modest, yielding, and devoted to learning.

sentences.zh: 年七歲時，母阮淑媛嘗病危篤，請僧行道。

translations.literal: At age seven, his mother Lady Ruan the Graceful Fair One was once gravely ill; [he] invited monks to perform rites.
translations.idiomatic: When he was seven, his mother Lady Ruan the Graceful Fair One fell gravely ill, and he invited monks to perform Buddhist rites on her behalf.

sentences.zh: 有獻蓮華供佛者，眾僧以銅罌盛水漬其莖，欲華不萎。

translations.literal: Someone presented lotus flowers to offer the Buddha; the monks placed water in a copper jar to soak the stems, wishing the flowers not to wither.
translations.idiomatic: Someone presented lotus blossoms as an offering to the Buddha. The monks placed them in a copper jar of water to soak the stems, hoping to keep the flowers from wilting.

sentences.zh: 子懋流涕禮佛曰：「若使阿姨因此和勝，願諸佛令華竟齋不萎。

translations.literal: Zimao weeping bowed to the Buddha saying: "If my aunt might thereby recover fully, I pray all Buddhas let the flowers remain unwithered through the entire fast.
translations.idiomatic: Zimao bowed before the Buddha with tears streaming down his face and said, "If my dear aunt may recover her health through this, I pray that the Buddhas will keep these flowers fresh and unwithered for the entire seven-day fast.

sentences.zh: 」七日齋畢，華更鮮紅，視罌中稍有根須，當世稱其孝感。

translations.literal: " When the seven-day fast concluded, the flowers were more fresh and red; looking in the jar there were slight roots; the age praised this as filial responsiveness.
translations.idiomatic: " When the seven-day fast was complete, the flowers were fresher and redder than before, and slight roots could be seen in the jar. People of the day praised this as an act of filial devotion moving Heaven.

sentences.zh: 永明五年，為南兗州刺史、監五州軍事。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Yongming, he became Inspector of Southern Yan Province, overseeing military affairs of five provinces.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Yongming he was appointed Inspector of Southern Yan Province with oversight of military affairs in five provinces.

sentences.zh: 六年，徙監湘州刺史。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, he was transferred to oversee the Inspector of Xiang Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was transferred to oversee the Inspector of Xiang Province.

sentences.zh: 八年，撰春秋例苑三十卷，奏之，武帝敕付秘閣。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, he compiled thirty juan of Chunqiu Liyuan, submitted it; Emperor Wu ordered it deposited in the Secret Archive.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he compiled thirty juan of Chunqiu Liyuan and submitted it to the throne. Emperor Wu ordered it deposited in the Secret Archive.

sentences.zh: 十一年，為都督、雍州刺史，給鼓吹一部。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, he became Area Commander and Inspector of Yong Province, given one set of martial pipes and drums.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he was appointed Area Commander and Inspector of Yong Province and granted one set of martial pipes and drums.

sentences.zh: 豫章王喪服未畢，上以邊州須威望，許得奏之。

translations.literal: Prince of Yuzhang's mourning garments not yet completed; the emperor because the border province needed prestige permitted him to take up the post with memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Niao of Yuzhang's mourning period was not yet complete, but because the border province required a figure of authority, the emperor permitted Zimao to assume the post upon memorializing.

sentences.zh: 啟求所好書，武帝曰：「知汝常以書讀在心，足為深欣。

translations.literal: He memorialized requesting favorite books; Emperor Wu said: "Knowing you constantly keep reading in your heart, this deeply pleases me.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized requesting books he favored. Emperor Wu replied, "Knowing that you always keep reading close to your heart gives me deep pleasure.

sentences.zh: 」賜以杜預手所定左傳及古今善言。

translations.literal: " He was granted Du Yu's hand-edited Zuozhuan and ancient and modern fine words.
translations.idiomatic: " He was granted Du Yu's hand-edited Zuozhuan and a collection of fine sayings ancient and modern.

sentences.zh: 延興元年，加侍中。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yanxing, he was promoted to Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yanxing he was promoted to Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 聞鄱陽、隨郡二王見殺，欲起兵赴難，與參軍周英、防合陸超之議：「傳檄荊、郢，入討君側，事成則宗廟獲安，不成猶為義鬼。

translations.literal: Hearing the two kings of Poyang and Suijun were killed, he wished to raise troops to rush to aid; with Aide Zhou Ying and garrison commander Lu Chaozhi he discussed: "Proclaiming by dispatch to Jing and Ying, entering to punish those at the ruler's side—if the matter succeeds the ancestral temple gains peace; if not, still one becomes a righteous ghost.
translations.idiomatic: When he learned that the Princes of Poyang and Suijun had been killed, he wished to raise troops to their aid and discussed the matter with Aide Zhou Ying and garrison commander Lu Chaozhi: "Let us issue proclamations to Jing and Ying and march to punish the evil at the ruler's side. If we succeed, the ancestral temple will be secure; if we fail, we will still die as righteous spirits.

sentences.zh: 」防合董僧慧攘袂曰：「此州雖小，孝武亦嘗用之，今以勤王之師，橫長江，指北闕，以請郁林之過，誰能對之。

translations.literal: " Garrison commander Dong Sengui rolled up sleeves saying: "This province though small, Emperor Xiaowu also once used it; now with troops loyal to the sovereign, crossing the Yangzi, pointing at the northern gate, to demand an accounting for the wrongs of Emperor Yulin—who can oppose them?
translations.idiomatic: " Garrison commander Dong Sengui rolled up his sleeves and said, "This province may be small, but Emperor Xiaowu once made use of it too. With an army loyal to the throne, we can cross the Yangzi, march on the northern gate, and demand justice for the wrongs done to Emperor Yulin—who could stand against us?

sentences.zh: 」於是部分兵將，入匡社稷。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he deployed troops and officers, entering to restore the state altars.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon he deployed his troops and officers to restore the realm.

sentences.zh: 母阮在都，遣書欲密迎上，阮報同產弟于瑤之為計。

translations.literal: Mother Ruan was in the capital; she sent a letter wishing secretly to welcome her lord; Ruan consulted her full brother Yu Yaozhi for a plan.
translations.idiomatic: His mother Lady Ruan was in the capital and sent a letter proposing to secretly welcome him there. Lady Ruan consulted her full brother Yu Yaozhi for advice on the plan.

sentences.zh: 瑤之馳告明帝，於是纂嚴，遣中護軍王玄邈、平西將軍王廣之南北討，使軍主裴叔業與瑤之先襲尋陽，聲雲為郢府司馬。

translations.literal: Yaozhi galloped to inform Emperor Ming; thereupon [Ming] gathered troops, sent Central Guard Wang Xuanyao and Pacifying West General Wang Guangzhi to campaign north and south, ordered army commander Pei Shuye with Yaozhi first to surprise attack Xunyang, publicly claiming to be Ying prefecture's Staff Major.
translations.idiomatic: Yaozhi galloped to inform Emperor Ming. Ming thereupon mobilized his forces and sent Central Guard General Wang Xuanyao and Pacifying West General Wang Guangzhi to campaign from north and south, dispatching army commander Pei Shuye with Yaozhi to strike Xunyang first, publicly claiming to be the Staff Major of the Ying prefecture.

sentences.zh: 子懋知之，遣三百人守盆城。

translations.literal: Zimao knew this, sent three hundred men to hold Pencheng.
translations.idiomatic: When Zimao learned of this, he sent three hundred men to hold Pencheng.

sentences.zh: 叔業泝流直上，襲盆城。

translations.literal: Shuye went upstream straight up, surprised Pencheng.
translations.idiomatic: Shuye sailed upstream and took Pencheng by surprise.

sentences.zh: 子懋先已具船於稽亭渚，聞叔業得盆城，乃據州自衛。

translations.literal: Zimao had already prepared boats at Jiting Ford; hearing Shuye took Pencheng, then held the province in self-defense.
translations.idiomatic: Zimao had already prepared boats at Jiting Ford. When he heard that Shuye had taken Pencheng, he held the province in self-defense.

sentences.zh: 子懋部曲多雍土人，皆踴躍願奮，叔業畏之，遣於瑤之說子懋曰：「今還都，必無過憂，政當作散官，不失富貴也。」

translations.literal: Zimao's followers many were natives of Yong region, all leaped willing to fight; Shuye feared them, sent Yu Yaozhi to persuade Zimao: "If you return to capital now, surely no excessive worry—you will merely be made an inactive official, not losing wealth and honor."
translations.idiomatic: Many of Zimao's followers were natives of Yong Province, and all were eager to fight. Shuye, fearing them, sent Yu Yaozhi to persuade Zimao, saying, "If you return to the capital now, you will surely come to no serious harm—you will merely be given an inactive post and will not lose your wealth and rank."

sentences.zh: 子懋既不出兵攻叔業，眾情稍沮。

translations.literal: Zimao since he did not go out to attack Shuye, the troops' spirits gradually sank.
translations.idiomatic: Since Zimao did not march out to attack Shuye, the troops' morale gradually sank.

sentences.zh: 中兵參軍於琳之，瑤之兄也，說子懋重賂叔業。

translations.literal: Central Army Aide Yu Linzhi, Yaozhi's elder brother, advised Zimao to heavily bribe Shuye.
translations.idiomatic: Central Army Aide Yu Linzhi, Yaozhi's elder brother, urged Zimao to bribe Shuye heavily.

sentences.zh: 子懋使琳之往，琳之因說叔業請取子懋。

translations.literal: Zimao sent Linzhi; Linzhi then advised Shuye to seize Zimao.
translations.idiomatic: Zimao sent Linzhi on the mission, but Linzhi instead urged Shuye to seize Zimao.

sentences.zh: 叔業遣軍主徐玄慶將四百人隨琳之入城，僚佐皆奔散，唯周英及外兵參軍王皎更移入城內。

translations.literal: Shuye sent army commander Xu Xuanqing leading four hundred men following Linzhi into the city; staff all fled scattered; only Zhou Ying and External Army Aide Wang Jiao moved further into the city.
translations.idiomatic: Shuye sent army commander Xu Xuanqing with four hundred men to follow Linzhi into the city. The staff all fled, but Zhou Ying and External Army Aide Wang Jiao moved deeper into the city instead.

sentences.zh: 子懋聞之歎曰：「不意吾府有義士二人。

translations.literal: Zimao heard and sighed: "I did not expect my headquarters to have two righteous men.
translations.idiomatic: When Zimao heard of this he sighed and said, "I never expected my headquarters to hold two men of such loyalty.

sentences.zh: 」琳之從二百人仗自入齋，子懋笑謂之曰：「不意渭陽，翻成梟鏡。

translations.literal: " Linzhi with two hundred men armed entered the study himself; Zimao smiled and said to him: "I did not expect Weiyang affection to turn into owl-and-mirror [betrayal].
translations.idiomatic: " Linzhi entered the study at the head of two hundred armed men. Zimao smiled at him and said, "I never thought the bond of Weiyang would become the treachery of the owl before the mirror.

sentences.zh: 」琳之以袖障面，使人害之。

translations.literal: " Linzhi covered his face with his sleeve, had men kill him.
translations.idiomatic: " Linzhi covered his face with his sleeve and had his men kill Zimao.

sentences.zh: 故人懼罪無敢至者，唯英、皎、僧慧號哭盡哀，為之喪殯。

translations.literal: Old associates fearing guilt none dared approach; only Ying, Jiao, and Sengui wailed with full grief, performed funeral rites for him.
translations.idiomatic: His old associates, fearing punishment, dared not come near; only Ying, Jiao, and Sengui wailed with full grief and performed funeral rites for him.

sentences.zh: 董僧慧，丹陽姑孰人，出自寒微而慷慨有節義。

translations.literal: Dong Sengui, native of Gushu in Danyang, from humble origins yet magnanimous with integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Sengui was a native of Gushu in Danyang. Though he came from humble origins, he was magnanimous and possessed a strong sense of honor.

sentences.zh: 好讀書，甚驍果，能反手於背彎五斛弓，當世莫有能者。

translations.literal: He loved reading, was very fierce and resolute, could from behind his back bend a five-hu bow; in the age none could match him.
translations.idiomatic: He loved to read and was exceptionally fierce and resolute. He could bend a five-hu bow behind his back, and none in his day could match him.

sentences.zh: 玄邈知其豫子懋之謀，執之。

translations.literal: Xuanyao knew he participated in Zimao's plot, arrested him.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanyao learned that he had taken part in Zimao's plot and arrested him.

sentences.zh: 僧慧曰：「晉安舉義兵，僕實豫議。

translations.literal: Sengui said: "When the Prince of Jin'an raised righteous troops, I indeed participated in the deliberations.
translations.idiomatic: Sengui said, "When the Prince of Jin'an raised his righteous army, I did indeed take part in the deliberations.

sentences.zh: 古人云'非死之難，得死之難'。

translations.literal: The ancients said, 'It is not dying that is hard—it is obtaining death that is hard.'
translations.idiomatic: The ancients said, 'It is not dying that is hard—it is obtaining death that is hard.'

sentences.zh: 僕得為主人死，不恨矣。

translations.literal: I obtain to die for my lord—I have no regret.
translations.idiomatic: To die for my lord—I have no regret.

sentences.zh: 願至主人大斂畢，退就湯鑊，雖死猶生。

translations.literal: I wish when my lord's great encoffining is complete, to withdraw and submit to the boiling cauldron—though dead, it would be as living.
translations.idiomatic: I ask only to attend my lord's full funeral rites, and then submit myself to the boiling cauldron. Though I die, it will be as though I live.

sentences.zh: 」玄邈義而許之。

translations.literal: " Xuanyao honored this and consented.
translations.idiomatic: " Xuanyao, moved by his integrity, consented.

sentences.zh: 還具白明帝，乃配東冶。

translations.literal: Returning he fully reported to Emperor Ming; [Sengui] was then assigned to Eastern Works [prison].
translations.idiomatic: When he returned he reported fully to Emperor Ming, and Sengui was assigned to the Eastern Works prison.

sentences.zh: 言及九江時事，輒悲不自勝。

translations.literal: Speaking of Jiujiang affairs, always grieved unable to restrain himself.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he spoke of the events at Jiujiang, he grieved beyond bearing.

sentences.zh: 子懋子昭基，九歲，以方二寸絹為書，參其消息，並遺錢五百，以金假人，崎嶇得至。

translations.literal: Zimao's son Zhaoji, nine years old, with a square two-inch silk wrote a letter inquiring of news, also sent five hundred coins; using gold hired a man; through hardship reached [him].
translations.idiomatic: Zimao's son Zhaoji, nine years old, wrote a letter on a square of silk two inches across inquiring after news, and sent five hundred coins as well. He used gold to hire a man, who made the arduous journey to deliver them.

sentences.zh: 僧慧睹書，對錢曰：「此郎君書也。

translations.literal: Sengui saw the letter; facing the coins said: "This is the young lord's letter.
translations.idiomatic: When Sengui saw the letter, he said to the coins beside it, "This is the young lord's writing.

sentences.zh: 」悲慟而卒。

translations.literal: " Grieved and anguished, died.
translations.idiomatic: " Overcome with grief, he died.

sentences.zh: 陸超之，吳人，以清靜雅為子懋所知。

translations.literal: Lu Chaozhi, a man of Wu, was known to Zimao for his quiet elegance.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Chaozhi was a man of Wu, known to Zimao for his quiet refinement.

sentences.zh: 子懋既敗，於琳之勸其逃亡。

translations.literal: After Zimao was defeated, Yu Linzhi urged him to flee.
translations.idiomatic: After Zimao was defeated, Yu Linzhi urged him to flee.

sentences.zh: 答曰：「人皆有死，此不足懼。

translations.literal: He replied: "All men must die—this is nothing to fear.
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "All men must die. That is nothing to fear.

sentences.zh: 吾若逃亡，非唯孤晉安之眷，亦恐田橫客笑人。

translations.literal: If I flee, I would not only fail those who rely on the Prince of Jin'an, but also fear that Tian Heng's followers would laugh at me.
translations.idiomatic: If I flee, I will not only fail those who depend on the Prince of Jin'an, but I also fear that Tian Heng's followers will laugh at me.

sentences.zh: 」玄邈等以其義，欲囚將還都，而超之亦端坐待命。

translations.literal: " Xuanyao and the others, impressed by his integrity, wished to imprison him and escort him back to the capital, but Chaozhi also sat upright awaiting his fate.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanyao and the others, moved by his integrity, wished to imprison him and escort him back to the capital, but Chaozhi simply sat upright and awaited his fate.

sentences.zh: 超之門生姓周者，謂殺超之當得賞，乃伺超之坐，自後斬之，頭墜而身不僵。

translations.literal: One of Chaozhi's disciples surnamed Zhou, believing that killing Chaozhi would win a reward, waited until Chaozhi was seated and struck him down from behind; his head fell but his body did not stiffen.
translations.idiomatic: One of Chaozhi's disciples surnamed Zhou, believing that killing Chaozhi would win a reward, waited until Chaozhi was seated and struck him down from behind. His head fell, but his body did not stiffen.

sentences.zh: 玄邈嘉其節，厚為殯斂。

translations.literal: Xuanyao admired his integrity and gave him a generous burial.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanyao admired his integrity and gave him a generous burial.

sentences.zh: 周又助舉棺，未出戶，棺墜，政壓其頭折頸即死。

translations.literal: Zhou also helped lift the coffin; before it passed through the doorway the coffin fell, crushing his head and breaking his neck—he died instantly.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou also helped lift the coffin, but before it passed through the doorway the coffin fell, crushing his head and breaking his neck. He died on the spot.

sentences.zh: 聞之者莫不以為有天道焉。

translations.literal: All who heard of it took it as Heaven's justice.
translations.idiomatic: All who heard of it took it as Heaven's justice.

sentences.zh: 隨郡王子隆字雲興，武帝第八子也。

translations.literal: Xiao Zilong, Prince of Suizhou, courtesy name Yunxing, was the eighth son of Emperor Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Zilong, Prince of Suizhou, courtesy name Yunxing, was the eighth son of Emperor Wu.

sentences.zh: 性和美，有文才。

translations.literal: His nature was gentle and pleasant, and he had literary talent.
translations.idiomatic: His nature was gentle and pleasant, and he had literary talent.

sentences.zh: 娶尚書令王儉女為妃。

translations.literal: He took the daughter of Minister of Works Wang Jian as his consort.
translations.idiomatic: He took the daughter of Minister of Works Wang Jian as his consort.

sentences.zh: 武帝以子隆能屬文，謂儉曰：「我家東阿也。」

translations.literal: Because Zilong could compose literary pieces, Emperor Wu told Jian, "In our house we have our own Cao Zhi."
translations.idiomatic: Because Zilong could compose literary pieces, Emperor Wu told Jian, "In our house we have our own Cao Zhi."

sentences.zh: 永明八年，為都督、荊州刺史。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Yongming he became Area Commander and Inspector of Jing Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Yongming he became Area Commander and Inspector of Jing Province.

sentences.zh: 隆昌元年，為侍中、撫軍將軍，領兵置佐。

translations.literal: In the first year of Longchang he became Palace Attendant and General Who Pacifies the Army, commanding troops with full staff.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Longchang he became Palace Attendant and General Who Pacifies the Army, commanding troops with full staff.

sentences.zh: 延興元年，轉中軍大將軍，侍中如故。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yanxing he was transferred to General-in-Chief of the Central Army, retaining his post as Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yanxing he was transferred to General-in-Chief of the Central Army, retaining his post as Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 子隆年二十一，而體過充壯，常使徐嗣伯合蘆茹丸以服自銷損，猶無益。

translations.literal: Zilong was twenty-one, yet his physique was excessively robust; he continually had Xu Sibo compound luru pills for him to take in hopes of reducing his weight, but to no avail.
translations.idiomatic: Zilong was twenty-one, yet his physique was excessively robust. He continually had Xu Sibo compound luru pills for him to take in hopes of slimming down, but to no avail.

sentences.zh: 明帝輔政，謀害諸王，武帝諸子中子隆最以才貌見憚，故與鄱陽王鏘同夜先見殺。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming served as regent and plotted to eliminate the princes, among Emperor Wu's sons Zilong was most feared for his talent and appearance; therefore he and Xiao Ziqiang, Prince of Poyang, were the first killed on the same night.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming served as regent and plotted to eliminate the princes, Zilong was the most feared among Emperor Wu's sons for his talent and appearance. He and Xiao Ziqiang, Prince of Poyang, were therefore the first to be killed, on the same night.

sentences.zh: 文集行於世。

translations.literal: His collected writings circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His collected writings circulated in the world.

sentences.zh: 建安王子真字雲仙，武帝第九子也。

translations.literal: Xiao Zizhen, Prince of Jian'an, courtesy name Yunxian, was the ninth son of Emperor Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Zizhen, Prince of Jian'an, courtesy name Yunxian, was the ninth son of Emperor Wu.

sentences.zh: 永明七年，累遷郢州刺史，加都督。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Yongming he was repeatedly promoted to Inspector of Ying Province and given the additional title of Area Commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Yongming he was repeatedly promoted to Inspector of Ying Province and given the additional title of Area Commander.

sentences.zh: 隆昌元年，為散騎常侍、護軍將軍。

translations.literal: In the first year of Longchang he became Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and General Who Guards the Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Longchang he became Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and General Who Guards the Army.

sentences.zh: 延興元年，明帝遣裴叔業就典簽柯令孫殺之，子真走入床下，令孫手牽出之，叩頭乞為奴贖死，不從，見害，年十九。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yanxing, Emperor Ming sent Pei Shuye to have chief clerk Ke Lingsun kill him; Zizhen fled under the bed, and Lingsun pulled him out by hand. He kowtowed and begged to be made a slave in exchange for his life, but was refused and killed. He was nineteen.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yanxing, Emperor Ming sent Pei Shuye to have chief clerk Ke Lingsun kill him. Zizhen fled under the bed, and Lingsun pulled him out by hand. He kowtowed and begged to be made a slave in exchange for his life, but was refused and killed. He was nineteen.

sentences.zh: 西陽王子明字雲光，武帝第十子也。

translations.literal: Xiao Ziming, Prince of Xiyang, courtesy name Yunguang, was the tenth son of Emperor Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Ziming, Prince of Xiyang, courtesy name Yunguang, was the tenth son of Emperor Wu.

sentences.zh: 永明元年，封武昌王。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongming he was enfeoffed as Prince of Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yongming he was enfeoffed as Prince of Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 三年，失國璽，改封西陽。

translations.literal: In the third year he lost the state seal and was re-enfeoffed as Prince of Xiyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he lost the state seal and was re-enfeoffed as Prince of Xiyang.

sentences.zh: 十年，為會稽太守，督五郡軍事。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he became Administrator of Kuaiji and supervised military affairs in five commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he became Administrator of Kuaiji and supervised military affairs in five commanderies.

sentences.zh: 子明風姿明淨，士女觀者，咸嗟歎之。

translations.literal: Ziming's bearing was bright and pure; men and women who watched him all sighed in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: Ziming's bearing was bright and pure; men and women who saw him all sighed in admiration.

sentences.zh: 建武元年，為撫軍將軍，領兵置佐。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jianwu he became General Who Pacifies the Army, commanding troops with full staff.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jianwu he became General Who Pacifies the Army, commanding troops with full staff.

sentences.zh: 二年，誅蕭諶，子明及弟子罕、子貞同諶謀見害，年十七。

translations.literal: In the second year, when Xiao Chen was executed, Ziming, his nephew Zihan, and Zizhen were killed for plotting with Chen. He was seventeen.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, when Xiao Chen was executed, Ziming, his nephew Zihan, and Zizhen were killed for plotting with Chen. He was seventeen.

sentences.zh: 南海王子罕字雲華，武帝第十一子也，頗有學。

translations.literal: Xiao Zihan, Prince of Nanhai, courtesy name Yunhua, was the eleventh son of Emperor Wu and was quite learned.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Zihan, Prince of Nanhai, courtesy name Yunhua, was the eleventh son of Emperor Wu and was quite learned.

sentences.zh: 母樂容華有寵，故武帝留心。

translations.literal: His mother, Lady Yue Ronghua, enjoyed favor, and so Emperor Wu kept him in mind.
translations.idiomatic: His mother, Lady Yue Ronghua, enjoyed favor, and so Emperor Wu kept him in mind.

sentences.zh: 母嘗寢疾，子罕晝夜祈禱。

translations.literal: When his mother once fell ill, Zihan prayed day and night.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother once fell ill, Zihan prayed day and night.

sentences.zh: 于時以竹為燈纘照夜，此纘宿昔枝葉大茂，母病亦愈，咸以為孝感所致。

translations.literal: At the time a bamboo lamp-wick was used to light the night; overnight its branches and leaves flourished greatly, and his mother's illness also recovered—all took it as the result of filial response.
translations.idiomatic: At the time a bamboo lamp-wick was used to light the night. Overnight its branches and leaves flourished greatly, and his mother's illness also recovered. All took it as the result of filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 主簿劉鬷及侍讀賀子喬為之賦頌，當時以為美談。

translations.literal: Chief Clerk Liu Juan and Lecturer He Ziqiao composed rhapsodies and eulogies for this; at the time it was regarded as a fine story.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Clerk Liu Juan and Lecturer He Ziqiao composed rhapsodies and eulogies for this, and at the time it was regarded as a fine story.

sentences.zh: 建武元年，位護軍將軍。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jianwu he held the post of General Who Guards the Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jianwu he held the post of General Who Guards the Army.

sentences.zh: 二年，見殺，年十七。

translations.literal: In the second year he was killed. He was seventeen.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was killed. He was seventeen.

sentences.zh: 巴陵王子倫字雲宗，武帝第十三子也。

translations.literal: Xiao Zilun, Prince of Baling, courtesy name Yunzong, was the thirteenth son of Emperor Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Zilun, Prince of Baling, courtesy name Yunzong, was the thirteenth son of Emperor Wu.

sentences.zh: 永明十年，為北中郎將、南琅邪彭城二郡太守。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Yongming he became General of the North Center and Administrator of the two commanderies of Southern Langye and Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Yongming he became General of the North Center and Administrator of the two commanderies of Southern Langye and Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 郁林即位，以南彭城祿力優厚，奪子倫與中書舍人綦母珍之，更以南蘭陵代之。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Yulin ascended the throne, because the revenue of Southern Pengcheng was rich and generous, he took it from Zilun and gave it to Palace Attendant Qimu Zhenzhi, replacing it with Southern Lanling.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Yulin ascended the throne, because the revenue of Southern Pengcheng was rich and generous, he took it from Zilun and gave it to Palace Attendant Qimu Zhenzhi, replacing it with Southern Lanling.

sentences.zh: 延興元年，明帝遣中書舍人茹法亮殺子倫，子倫時鎮琅邪城，有守兵，子倫英果，明帝恐不即罪，以問典簽華伯茂。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yanxing, Emperor Ming sent Palace Attendant Ru Faliang to kill Zilun. Zilun was then stationed at Langye city and had garrison troops; he was bold and resolute. Emperor Ming feared he could not be punished immediately and asked chief clerk Hua Bomao about it.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yanxing, Emperor Ming sent Palace Attendant Ru Faliang to kill Zilun. Zilun was then stationed at Langye city and had garrison troops; he was bold and resolute. Emperor Ming feared he could not be punished immediately and asked chief clerk Hua Bomao about it.

sentences.zh: 伯茂曰：「公若遣兵取之，恐不即可辦，若委伯茂，一小吏力耳。

translations.literal: Bomao said: "If Your Grace sends troops to take him, I fear it cannot be done at once. If you entrust it to Bomao, it is but the strength of one petty clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Bomao said, "If Your Grace sends troops to take him, I fear it cannot be done at once. If you entrust it to me, it is but the strength of one petty clerk.

sentences.zh: 」既而伯茂手自執鴆逼之，左右莫敢動者。

translations.literal: " Thereupon Bomao personally held poisoned wine and forced it on him; none of those around dared move.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Bomao personally held poisoned wine and forced it on him, and none of those around dared move.

sentences.zh: 子倫正衣冠，出受詔，謂法亮曰：「積不善之家，必有餘殃。

translations.literal: Zilun straightened his cap and robes, came out to receive the edict, and said to Faliang: "A house that accumulates no goodness is sure to have surplus calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Zilun straightened his cap and robes, came out to receive the edict, and said to Faliang, "A house that accumulates no goodness is sure to have surplus calamity.

sentences.zh: 昔高皇帝殘滅劉氏；

translations.literal: In former times the Gao Emperor exterminated the Liu clan;
translations.idiomatic: In former times the Gao Emperor exterminated the Liu clan;

sentences.zh: 今日之事，理數固然。

translations.literal: Today's affair is the natural course of principle and fate.
translations.idiomatic: Today's affair is the natural course of principle and fate.

sentences.zh: 」舉酒謂法亮曰：「君是身家舊人，今銜此命，當由事不獲已。

translations.literal: " He raised a cup and said to Faliang: "You are an old retainer of our household. Now you carry this command—it must be because the matter cannot be helped.
translations.idiomatic: " He raised a cup and said to Faliang, "You are an old retainer of our household. Now you carry this command—it must be because the matter cannot be helped.

sentences.zh: 此酒差非勸酬之爵。

translations.literal: This wine is hardly a cup for a toast of encouragement.
translations.idiomatic: This wine is hardly a cup for a toast of encouragement.

sentences.zh: 」因仰之而死，時年十六，法亮及左右皆流涕。

translations.literal: " He then raised it and drank, and died. He was sixteen. Faliang and those around him all wept.
translations.idiomatic: " He then raised it and drank, and died. He was sixteen. Faliang and those around him all wept.

sentences.zh: 先是高帝、武帝為諸王置典簽帥，一方之事，悉以委之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Emperor Gao and Emperor Wu had established chief clerk commanders for the princes, and all affairs of a region were entrusted to them.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Emperor Gao and Emperor Wu had established chief clerk commanders for the princes, and all affairs of a region were entrusted to them.

sentences.zh: 每至覲接，輒留心顧問，刺史行事之美惡，系於典簽之口，莫不折節推奉，恒慮弗及，於是威行州部，權重蕃君。

translations.literal: Whenever the princes came to court, the emperor would carefully inquire after them; whether a governor's conduct was good or bad depended on the chief clerk's word. None failed to defer and flatter him, always fearing they fell short—thus his authority ran through the province, and his power outweighed that of the feudal lord.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the princes came to court, the emperor would carefully inquire after them. Whether a governor's conduct was good or bad depended on the chief clerk's word. None failed to defer and flatter him, always fearing they fell short—thus his authority ran through the province, and his power outweighed that of the feudal lord.

sentences.zh: 武陵王曄為江州，性烈直不可忤，典簽趙渥之曰：「今出都易刺史。

translations.literal: When Xiao Ye, Prince of Wuling, was in Jiang Province, his nature was fierce and upright and brooked no offense. Chief clerk Zhao Wozhi said: "One who leaves the capital can easily replace a provincial inspector.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao Ye, Prince of Wuling, was in Jiang Province, his nature was fierce and upright and brooked no offense. Chief clerk Zhao Wozhi said, "One who leaves the capital can easily replace a provincial inspector.

sentences.zh: 」及見武帝相誣，曄遂免還。

translations.literal: " When he saw Emperor Wu he slandered Ye, and Ye was dismissed and recalled.
translations.idiomatic: When he saw Emperor Wu he slandered Ye, and Ye was dismissed and recalled.

sentences.zh: 南海王子罕戍琅邪，欲暫遊東堂，典簽薑秀不許而止。

translations.literal: Xiao Zihan, Prince of Nanhai, was garrisoned at Langye and wished to stroll briefly to the Eastern Hall, but chief clerk Jiang Xiu would not permit it, so he stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Zihan, Prince of Nanhai, was garrisoned at Langye and wished to stroll briefly to the Eastern Hall, but chief clerk Jiang Xiu would not permit it, so he stopped.

sentences.zh: 還泣謂母曰：「兒欲移五步亦不得，與囚何異。

translations.literal: On returning he wept and told his mother: "My son wishes to move five paces and cannot—how is this different from being a prisoner?
translations.idiomatic: On returning he wept and told his mother, "My son wishes to move five paces and cannot—how is this different from being a prisoner?

sentences.zh: 」秀後輒取子罕屐傘飲器等供其兒昏，武帝知之，鞭二百，系尚方，然而擅命不改。

translations.literal: " Later Xiu repeatedly took Zihan's sandals, umbrella, drinking vessels, and the like to supply his son's wedding. When Emperor Wu learned of it he had Xiu flogged two hundred strokes and assigned to the Directorate of Manufactories, yet his arbitrary commands did not change.
translations.idiomatic: Later Xiu repeatedly took Zihan's sandals, umbrella, drinking vessels, and the like to supply his son's wedding. When Emperor Wu learned of it he had Xiu flogged two hundred strokes and assigned to the Directorate of Manufactories, yet his arbitrary commands did not change.

sentences.zh: 邵陵王子貞嘗求熊白，廚人答典簽不在，不敢與。

translations.literal: Xiao Zizhen, Prince of Shaoling, once asked for bear's paw marrow; the cook replied that the chief clerk was away and dared not give it.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Zizhen, Prince of Shaoling, once asked for bear's paw marrow; the cook replied that the chief clerk was away and dared not give it.

sentences.zh: 西陽王子明欲送書參侍讀鮑僎病，典簽吳修之不許，曰：「應諮行事。

translations.literal: Xiao Ziming, Prince of Xiyang, wished to send a letter to visit Lecturer Bao Fu, who was ill; chief clerk Wu Xiuzhi would not permit it and said: "One should consult the acting governor.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Ziming, Prince of Xiyang, wished to send a letter to visit Lecturer Bao Fu, who was ill; chief clerk Wu Xiuzhi would not permit it and said, "One should consult the acting governor.

sentences.zh: 」乃止。

translations.literal: " He then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: He then stopped.

sentences.zh: 言行舉動，不得自專，征衣求食，必須諮訪。

translations.literal: In word, deed, and movement they could not act on their own; for clothes or food they had to seek permission.
translations.idiomatic: In word, deed, and movement they could not act on their own; for clothes or food they had to seek permission.

sentences.zh: 永明中，巴東王子響殺行事劉寅等，武帝聞之，謂群臣曰：「子響遂反。

translations.literal: In the Yongming era, Xiao Zixiang, Marquis of Yufu, killed Acting Governor Liu Yin and others. When Emperor Wu heard of it he told the assembled ministers: "Zixiang has truly rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yongming era, Xiao Zixiang, Marquis of Yufu, killed Acting Governor Liu Yin and others. When Emperor Wu heard of it he told the assembled ministers, "Zixiang has truly rebelled.

sentences.zh: 」戴僧靜大言曰：「諸王都自應反，豈唯巴東。

translations.literal: " Dai Sengjing spoke up loudly: "All the princes ought naturally to rebel—why only Badong?
translations.idiomatic: Dai Sengjing spoke up loudly, "All the princes ought naturally to rebel—why only Badong?

sentences.zh: 」武帝問其故，答曰：「天王無罪，而一時被囚，取一挺藕，一杯漿，皆諮簽帥，不在則竟日忍渴。

translations.literal: " Emperor Wu asked the reason, and he replied: "The princes are innocent, yet for a time they are imprisoned. To take one lotus root or one cup of gruel, they must consult the chief clerk commander; if he is absent they endure thirst all day.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu asked the reason, and he replied, "The princes are innocent, yet for a time they are imprisoned. To take one lotus root or one cup of gruel, they must consult the chief clerk commander; if he is absent they endure thirst all day.

sentences.zh: 諸州唯聞有簽帥，不聞有刺史。」

translations.literal: In the provinces one hears only of chief clerk commanders, not of provincial inspectors."
translations.idiomatic: In the provinces one hears only of chief clerk commanders, not of provincial inspectors."

sentences.zh: 竟陵王子良嘗問眾曰：「士大夫何意詣簽帥？

translations.literal: Xiao Ziliang, Prince Wenxuan of Jingling, once asked the assembly: "What do the gentry mean by calling on the chief clerk commander?
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Ziliang, Prince Wenxuan of Jingling, once asked the assembly, "What do the gentry mean by calling on the chief clerk commander?

sentences.zh: 」參軍範雲答曰：「詣長史以下皆無益，詣簽帥便有倍本之價，不詣謂何！

translations.literal: " Aide Fan Yun replied: "Calling on anyone below the chief secretary is useless; calling on the chief clerk commander doubles the principal—why not call on him!
translations.idiomatic: Aide Fan Yun replied, "Calling on anyone below the chief secretary is useless; calling on the chief clerk commander doubles the principal—why not call on him!

sentences.zh: 」子良有愧色。

translations.literal: " Ziliang showed a look of shame.
translations.idiomatic: Ziliang showed a look of shame.

sentences.zh: 及明帝誅異己者，諸王見害，悉典簽所殺，竟無一人相抗。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming executed those who differed from him, the princes who were killed were all slain by chief clerks—not one resisted.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming executed those who differed from him, the princes who were killed were all slain by chief clerks—not one resisted.

sentences.zh: 孔珪聞之流涕曰：「齊之衡陽、江夏最有意，而復害之。

translations.literal: Kong Gui heard of it and wept, saying: "Among Qi's princes, Hengyang and Jiangxia had the most spirit, yet they were killed again.
translations.idiomatic: When Kong Gui heard of it he wept and said, "Among Qi's princes, Hengyang and Jiangxia had the most spirit, yet they were killed again.

sentences.zh: 若不立簽帥，故當不至於此。」

translations.literal: Had chief clerk commanders not been established, things would surely not have come to this."
translations.idiomatic: Had chief clerk commanders not been established, things would surely not have come to this."

sentences.zh: 邵陵王子貞字雲松，武帝第十四子也。

translations.literal: Xiao Zizhen, Prince of Shaoling, courtesy name Yunsong, was the fourteenth son of Emperor Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Zizhen, Prince of Shaoling, courtesy name Yunsong, was the fourteenth son of Emperor Wu.

sentences.zh: 建武二年見誅，年十五。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianwu he was executed. He was fifteen.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jianwu he was executed. He was fifteen.

sentences.zh: 臨賀王子岳字雲嶠，武帝第十六子也。

translations.literal: Xiao Ziyue, Prince of Linhe, courtesy name Yunqiao, was the sixteenth son of Emperor Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Ziyue, Prince of Linhe, courtesy name Yunqiao, was the sixteenth son of Emperor Wu.

sentences.zh: 明帝誅武帝諸子，唯子岳及弟六人在後，時呼為「七王」。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming executed Emperor Wu's sons, only Ziyue and six younger brothers remained; at the time they were called the "Seven Princes."
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming executed Emperor Wu's sons, only Ziyue and six younger brothers remained; at the time they were called the "Seven Princes."

sentences.zh: 朔望入朝，上還後宮，輒歎息曰：「我及司徒諸兒子皆不長，高、武子孫日長大。

translations.literal: On the first and fifteenth of each month when they entered court, after the emperor returned to the inner palace he would sigh and say: "My sons and the Minister's sons are all still young, while Gao and Wu's descendants grow day by day.
translations.idiomatic: On the first and fifteenth of each month when they entered court, after the emperor returned to the inner palace he would sigh and say, "My sons and the Minister's sons are all still young, while Gao and Wu's descendants grow day by day.

sentences.zh: 」永泰元年，上疾甚，絕而復蘇，於是誅子嶽等。

translations.literal: " In the first year of Yongtai the emperor fell gravely ill, stopped breathing and then revived; thereupon Ziyue and the others were executed.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yongtai the emperor fell gravely ill, stopped breathing and then revived; thereupon Ziyue and the others were executed.

sentences.zh: 延興、建武中，凡三誅諸王，每一行事，明帝輒先燒香，嗚咽涕泣，眾以此輒知其夜當殺戮也。

translations.literal: During Yanxing and Jianwu, the princes were executed three times in all; before each affair Emperor Ming would first burn incense, sobbing and weeping, and the crowd thereby always knew that he would kill that night.
translations.idiomatic: During Yanxing and Jianwu, the princes were executed three times in all. Before each affair Emperor Ming would first burn incense, sobbing and weeping, and the crowd thereby always knew that he would kill that night.

sentences.zh: 子岳死時年十四。

translations.literal: When Ziyue died he was fourteen.
translations.idiomatic: When Ziyue died he was fourteen.

sentences.zh: 西陽王子文字雲儒，武帝第十七子也。

translations.literal: Xiao Ziwen, Prince of Xiyang, courtesy name Yunru, was the seventeenth son of Emperor Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Ziwen, Prince of Xiyang, courtesy name Yunru, was the seventeenth son of Emperor Wu.

sentences.zh: 永明七年，封蜀郡王，建武中，改封西陽。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Yongming he was enfeoffed as Prince of Shujun; in the Jianwu era he was re-enfeoffed as Prince of Xiyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Yongming he was enfeoffed as Prince of Shujun; in the Jianwu era he was re-enfeoffed as Prince of Xiyang.

sentences.zh: 永泰元年見殺，年十四。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongtai he was killed. He was fourteen.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yongtai he was killed. He was fourteen.

sentences.zh: 衡陽王子峻字雲嵩，武帝第十八子也。

translations.literal: Xiao Zijun, Prince of Hengyang, courtesy name Yunsong, was the eighteenth son of Emperor Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Zijun, Prince of Hengyang, courtesy name Yunsong, was the eighteenth son of Emperor Wu.

sentences.zh: 永明七年，封廣漢郡王，建武中改封。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Yongming he was enfeoffed as Prince of Guanghan Commandery; in the Jianwu era his enfeoffment was changed.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Yongming he was enfeoffed as Prince of Guanghan Commandery; in the Jianwu era his enfeoffment was changed.

sentences.zh: 永泰元年見殺，年十四。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongtai he was killed. He was fourteen.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yongtai he was killed. He was fourteen.

sentences.zh: 南康王子琳字雲璋，武帝第十九子也。

translations.literal: Xiao Zilin, Prince of Nankang, courtesy name Yunzhang, was the nineteenth son of Emperor Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Zilin, Prince of Nankang, courtesy name Yunzhang, was the nineteenth son of Emperor Wu.

sentences.zh: 母荀昭華盛寵，後宮才人位登采女者，依例舊賜玉鳳凰，荀時始為采女，得玉鳳凰投地曰：「我不能例受此。

translations.literal: His mother, Lady Xun Zhaohua, enjoyed great favor. When palace talents were promoted by precedent to the rank of Selected Maid and were customarily granted jade phoenixes, Xun had only just become a Selected Maid; receiving a jade phoenix she cast it to the ground and said: "I cannot accept this by precedent.
translations.idiomatic: His mother, Lady Xun Zhaohua, enjoyed great favor.
