sentences.zh: 」武帝乃拜為昭華。

translations.literal: " Emperor Wu then invested her as Lady Zhaohua.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu then invested her as Lady Zhaohua.

sentences.zh: 子琳以母寵故最見愛。

translations.literal: Zilin was most beloved because of his mother's favor.
translations.idiomatic: Zilin was most beloved because of his mother's favor.

sentences.zh: 太尉王儉因請昏，武帝悅而許之。

translations.literal: Grand Commandant Wang Jian thereupon requested a marriage alliance, and Emperor Wu was pleased and consented.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Commandant Wang Jian thereupon requested a marriage alliance, and Emperor Wu was pleased and consented.

sentences.zh: 群臣奉寶物名好盡直數百金，武帝為之報答亦如此。

translations.literal: The assembled ministers presented famous treasures, all valued at several hundred gold; Emperor Wu's return gifts were likewise.
translations.idiomatic: The assembled ministers presented famous treasures, all valued at several hundred gold; Emperor Wu's return gifts were likewise.

sentences.zh: 及應封，而好郡已盡，乃以宣城封之。

translations.literal: When the time came for enfeoffment, the desirable commanderies were already exhausted, and so Xuancheng was used to enfeoff him.
translations.idiomatic: When the time came for enfeoffment, the desirable commanderies were already exhausted, and so Xuancheng was used to enfeoff him.

sentences.zh: 既而以宣城屬揚州，不欲為王國，改封南康公褚蓁為巴東公，以南康為王國封子琳。

translations.literal: Later, because Xuancheng belonged to Yang Province and was not desired as a princely state, Duke of Nankang Chu Zhen was re-enfeoffed as Duke of Badong, and Nankang was made a princely state to enfeoff Zilin.
translations.idiomatic: Later, because Xuancheng belonged to Yang Province and was not desired as a princely state, Duke of Nankang Chu Zhen was re-enfeoffed as Duke of Badong, and Nankang was made a princely state to enfeoff Zilin.

sentences.zh: 永泰元年見殺，年十四。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongtai he was killed. He was fourteen.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yongtai he was killed. He was fourteen.

sentences.zh: 湘東王子建字雲立，武帝第二十一子也。

translations.literal: Xiao Zijian, Prince of Xiangdong, courtesy name Yunli, was the twenty-first son of Emperor Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Zijian, Prince of Xiangdong, courtesy name Yunli, was the twenty-first son of Emperor Wu.

sentences.zh: 母謝無寵，武帝度為尼。

translations.literal: His mother, Lady Xie, had no favor; Emperor Wu had her ordained as a Buddhist nun.
translations.idiomatic: His mother, Lady Xie, had no favor; Emperor Wu had her ordained as a Buddhist nun.

sentences.zh: 明帝即位，使還母子建。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming ascended the throne he had her restored to Zijian.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming ascended the throne he had her restored to Zijian.

sentences.zh: 永泰元年見殺，年十三。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongtai he was killed. He was thirteen.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yongtai he was killed. He was thirteen.

sentences.zh: 南郡王子夏字雲廣，武帝第二十三子也。

translations.literal: Xiao Zixia, Prince of Nanjun, courtesy name Yunguang, was the twenty-third son of Emperor Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Zixia, Prince of Nanjun, courtesy name Yunguang, was the twenty-third son of Emperor Wu.

sentences.zh: 上春秋高，子夏最幼，寵愛過諸子。

translations.literal: The emperor was advanced in years, and Zixia was the youngest; he was favored beyond all the other sons.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was advanced in years, and Zixia was the youngest; he was favored beyond all the other sons.

sentences.zh: 初，武帝夢金翅鳥下殿庭，搏食小龍無數，乃飛上天。

translations.literal: Earlier, Emperor Wu dreamed that a golden-winged bird descended into the palace courtyard, seized and devoured countless small dragons, then flew up to heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Emperor Wu dreamed that a golden-winged bird descended into the palace courtyard, seized and devoured countless small dragons, then flew up to heaven.

sentences.zh: 及明帝初，其夢方驗。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming first came to power, the dream was fulfilled.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming first came to power, the dream was fulfilled.

sentences.zh: 永泰元年，子夏誅，年七歲。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongtai, Zixia was executed. He was seven.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yongtai, Zixia was executed. He was seven.

sentences.zh: 文惠太子四男：安皇后生廢帝郁林王昭業，宮人許氏生廢帝海陵恭王昭文，陳氏生巴陵王昭秀，褚氏生桂陽王昭粲。

translations.literal: Crown Prince Wenhui had four sons: Empress An bore the deposed Emperor Zhaoye, Prince of Yulin; palace woman Lady Xu bore the deposed Emperor Zhaowen, Prince Gong of Hailing; Lady Chen bore Zhaoxiu, Prince of Baling; Lady Chu bore Zhaocan, Prince of Guiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Wenhui had four sons. Empress An gave birth to the deposed Emperor Zhaoye, Prince of Yulin. A palace woman surnamed Xu bore the deposed Emperor Zhaowen, Prince Gong of Hailing. Lady Chen bore Zhaoxiu, Prince of Baling, and Lady Chu bore Zhaocan, Prince of Guiyang.

sentences.zh: 巴陵王昭秀字懷尚，太子第三子也。

translations.literal: Xiao Zhaoxiu, Prince of Baling, courtesy name Huaishang, was the crown prince's third son.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Zhaoxiu, Prince of Baling, courtesy name Huaishang, was the crown prince's third son.

sentences.zh: 郁林即位，封臨海郡王。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Yulin ascended the throne, he was enfeoffed as Prince of Linhai Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Yulin ascended the throne, Zhaoxiu was enfeoffed as Prince of Linhai Commandery.

sentences.zh: 隆昌元年，為都督、荊州刺史。

translations.literal: In the first year of Longchang he was made Area Commander and Governor of Jing Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Longchang he was made Area Commander and Governor of Jing Province.

sentences.zh: 延興元年，徵為車騎將軍。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yanxing he was summoned to serve as General of Chariots and Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yanxing he was recalled to serve as General of Chariots and Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 明帝建武二年，改封巴陵王。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianwu under Emperor Ming, he was re-enfeoffed as Prince of Baling.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jianwu, Emperor Ming re-enfeoffed him as Prince of Baling.

sentences.zh: 永泰元年見殺，年十六。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongtai he was killed. He was sixteen.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yongtai he was killed. He was sixteen.

sentences.zh: 桂陽王昭粲，太子第四子也。

translations.literal: Zhaocan, Prince of Guiyang, was the crown prince's fourth son.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaocan, Prince of Guiyang, was the crown prince's fourth son.

sentences.zh: 郁林立，封永嘉郡王。

translations.literal: When Yulin was established, he was enfeoffed as Prince of Yongjia Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Yulin was installed as emperor, Zhaocan was enfeoffed as Prince of Yongjia Commandery.

sentences.zh: 延興元年，出為荊州刺史，加都督。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yanxing he went out to serve as Governor of Jing Province and was given the additional title of Area Commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yanxing he was sent out as Governor of Jing Province with the additional title of Area Commander.

sentences.zh: 建武二年，改封桂陽王。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianwu his enfeoffment was changed to Prince of Guiyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jianwu his enfeoffment was changed to Prince of Guiyang.

sentences.zh: 四年，為太常。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was made Grand Minister of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was made Grand Minister of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 永泰元年見殺，年八歲。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongtai he was killed. He was eight.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yongtai he was killed. He was eight.

sentences.zh: 明帝十一男：敬皇后生廢帝東昏侯寶卷、江夏王寶玄、鄱陽王寶寅、和帝，殷貴嬪生巴陵隱王寶義、晉熙王寶嵩，袁貴妃生廬陵王寶源，管淑妃生邵陵王寶修，許淑媛生桂陽王寶貞。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming had eleven sons: Empress Jing bore the deposed Emperor Bao Juan, Marquis of Donghun; Prince Baoxuan of Jiangxia; Prince Baoyin of Poyang; and Emperor He; Noble Consort Yin bore Prince Bao Yi of Baling the Hidden; Prince Bao Song of Jinxi; Noble Consort Yuan bore Prince Baoyuan of Luling; Lady Guan Shufei bore Prince Baoxiu of Shaoling; Lady Xu Shuyuan bore Prince Bao Zhen of Guiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming had eleven sons. Empress Jing gave birth to the deposed Emperor Bao Juan, Marquis of Donghun; Prince Baoxuan of Jiangxia; Prince Baoyin of Poyang; and Emperor He. Noble Consort Yin bore Prince Bao Yi of Baling the Hidden and Prince Bao Song of Jinxi. Noble Consort Yuan bore Prince Baoyuan of Luling. Lady Guan Shufei bore Prince Baoxiu of Shaoling, and Lady Xu Shuyuan bore Prince Bao Zhen of Guiyang.

sentences.zh: 餘皆早夭。

translations.literal: The rest all died in infancy.
translations.idiomatic: The rest all died in infancy.

sentences.zh: 寶義少有廢疾，不堪出人間，止加除授，為都督、揚州刺史，仍以始安王遙光代之。

translations.literal: Bao Yi from youth had a crippling ailment and could not appear in public; he received only nominal appointments, was made Area Commander and Governor of Yang Province, and Prince Yaoguang of Shi'an was still sent to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: Bao Yi had suffered from a crippling ailment since youth and could not appear in public. He received only nominal appointments and was made Area Commander and Governor of Yang Province, but Prince Yaoguang of Shi'an was still sent to replace him.

sentences.zh: 轉為右將軍，領兵置佐，鎮石頭。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Right General, given troops and staff, and garrisoned at Stone City.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Right General, given troops and staff, and garrisoned at Stone City.

sentences.zh: 二年，為南徐州刺史，加都督。

translations.literal: In the second year he was made Governor of South Xu Province and given the additional title of Area Commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was made Governor of South Xu Province with the additional title of Area Commander.

sentences.zh: 東昏即位，進征北將軍、開府儀同三司，給扶。

translations.literal: When Emperor Donghun ascended the throne, he was promoted to General Who Conquers the North and Grand Preceptor with the same privileges as the Three Excellencies, and granted a supporting staff.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Donghun ascended the throne, he was promoted to General Who Conquers the North and Grand Preceptor Equal to the Three Excellencies, and granted a supporting staff.

sentences.zh: 永元元年，為都督、揚州刺史。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongyuan he was made Area Commander and Governor of Yang Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yongyuan he was made Area Commander and Governor of Yang Province.

sentences.zh: 三年，進位司徒。

translations.literal: In the third year he was promoted to the post of Minister over the Masses.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was promoted to Minister over the Masses.

sentences.zh: 和帝西台建，以為侍中、司空。

translations.literal: When the Western Platform was established under Emperor He, he was made Attendant-in-Ordinary and Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor He established the Western Platform, he was made Attendant-in-Ordinary and Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 江夏王寶玄字智深，明帝第三子也。

translations.literal: Xiao Baoxuan, Prince of Jiangxia, courtesy name Zhishen, was Emperor Ming's third son.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Baoxuan, Prince of Jiangxia, courtesy name Zhishen, was Emperor Ming's third son.

sentences.zh: 建武元年，封江夏郡王。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jianwu he was enfeoffed as Prince of Jiangxia Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jianwu he was enfeoffed as Prince of Jiangxia Commandery.

sentences.zh: 東昏即位，為都督、南徐兗二州刺史。

translations.literal: When Emperor Donghun ascended the throne, he was made Area Commander and Governor of South Xu and Yan Provinces.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Donghun ascended the throne, he was made Area Commander and Governor of South Xu and Yan Provinces.

sentences.zh: 寶玄娶尚書令徐孝嗣女為妃，孝嗣被誅離絕，東昏送少姬二人與之。

translations.literal: Baoxuan took as consort the daughter of Director of the Secretariat Xu Xiaosi. When Xiaosi was executed the marriage was severed; Donghun sent him two young concubines.
translations.idiomatic: Baoxuan had taken as consort the daughter of Director of the Secretariat Xu Xiaosi. When Xiaosi was executed the marriage was severed, and Donghun sent him two young concubines in her place.

sentences.zh: 寶玄恨望有異計。

translations.literal: Baoxuan harbored resentment and had disloyal designs.
translations.idiomatic: Baoxuan nursed resentment and began to plot treason.

sentences.zh: 明年，崔慧景舉兵，還至廣陵，遣使奉寶玄為主，寶玄斬其使，因是發將吏防城。

translations.literal: The following year Cui Huijing raised troops and returned to Guangling, sending envoys to install Baoxuan as leader. Baoxuan beheaded the envoys and thereupon mobilized officers and clerks to defend the city.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Cui Huijing raised troops and returned to Guangling, sending envoys to install Baoxuan as leader. Baoxuan beheaded the envoys and thereupon mobilized his officers and clerks to defend the city.

sentences.zh: 慧景將度江，寶玄密與相應，開門納慧景，乘八扛輿，手執絳麾幡，隨慧景至都，百姓多往投集。

translations.literal: As Huijing was about to cross the Yangzi, Baoxuan secretly coordinated with him, opened the gates to admit Huijing, rode in an eight-bearer palanquin, and holding a crimson command banner in hand followed Huijing to the capital; many commoners went to join them.
translations.idiomatic: As Huijing was about to cross the Yangzi, Baoxuan secretly coordinated with him, opened the gates to admit him, rode in an eight-bearer palanquin with a crimson command banner in hand, and followed Huijing to the capital. Many commoners went to join them.

sentences.zh: 慧景敗，收得朝野投寶玄及慧景軍名，東昏令燒之，曰：「江夏尚爾，豈復可罪餘人。」

translations.literal: When Huijing was defeated, they collected lists from court and countryside of those who had joined Baoxuan and Huijing's army. Donghun ordered them burned, saying: "If even the Prince of Jiangxia was like this, how could the others be punished?"
translations.idiomatic: When Huijing was defeated, officials collected lists from court and countryside of those who had joined Baoxuan and Huijing's army. Donghun ordered them burned, saying, "If even the Prince of Jiangxia was like this, how could the others be punished?"

sentences.zh: 寶玄逃奔，數日乃出，帝召入後堂，以步鄣裹之，令群小數十人鳴鼓角馳繞其外，遣人謂曰：「汝近圍我亦如此。

translations.literal: Baoxuan fled; after several days he came out. The emperor summoned him to the rear hall, wrapped him in portable screens, had several dozen ruffians sound drums and horns and gallop around outside, and sent someone to tell him: "When you recently besieged me it was just like this.
translations.idiomatic: Baoxuan fled, but after several days he came out. The emperor summoned him to the rear hall, wrapped him in portable screens, and had several dozen ruffians sound drums and horns as they galloped around outside. He sent someone to tell him, "When you recently besieged me it was just like this.

sentences.zh: 」少日乃殺之。

translations.literal: " A few days later he killed him.
translations.idiomatic: A few days later he killed him.

sentences.zh: 廬陵王寶源字智泉，明帝第五子也。

translations.literal: Xiao Baoyuan, Prince of Luling, courtesy name Zhiquan, was Emperor Ming's fifth son.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Baoyuan, Prince of Luling, courtesy name Zhiquan, was Emperor Ming's fifth son.

sentences.zh: 建武元年封。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed in the first year of Jianwu.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed in the first year of Jianwu.

sentences.zh: 和帝即位，為車騎將軍、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: When Emperor He ascended the throne, he was made General of Chariots and Cavalry and Grand Preceptor with the same privileges as the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor He ascended the throne, he was made General of Chariots and Cavalry and Grand Preceptor Equal to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 中興二年薨。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhongxing he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhongxing he died.

sentences.zh: 鄱陽王寶寅字智亮，明帝第六子也。

translations.literal: Xiao Baoyin, Prince of Poyang, courtesy name Zhiliang, was Emperor Ming's sixth son.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Baoyin, Prince of Poyang, courtesy name Zhiliang, was Emperor Ming's sixth son.

sentences.zh: 建武初，封建安郡王。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianwu he was enfeoffed as Prince of Jian'an Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Jianwu he was enfeoffed as Prince of Jian'an Commandery.

sentences.zh: 東昏即位，為都督、郢州刺史。

translations.literal: When Emperor Donghun ascended the throne, he was made Area Commander and Governor of Ying Province.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Donghun ascended the throne, he was made Area Commander and Governor of Ying Province.

sentences.zh: 永元三年，為車騎將軍、開府儀同三司，鎮石頭。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yongyuan he was made General of Chariots and Cavalry and Grand Preceptor with the same privileges as the Three Excellencies, and garrisoned Stone City.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yongyuan he was made General of Chariots and Cavalry and Grand Preceptor Equal to the Three Excellencies, and garrisoned Stone City.

sentences.zh: 其秋，雍州刺史張欣泰等謀起事於新亭，殺台內諸主帥。

translations.literal: That autumn Governor of Yong Province Zhang Xintai and others plotted to raise an affair at Xinting and kill the various commanders within the capital.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn Governor of Yong Province Zhang Xintai and others plotted to raise a revolt at Xinting and kill the various commanders within the capital.

sentences.zh: 難作之日，前南譙太守王靈秀奔往石頭，帥城內將吏，去車腳，載寶寅向台城，百姓數千人皆空手隨後。

translations.literal: On the day the trouble broke out, former Administrator of South Qiao Wang Lingxiu rushed to Stone City, led the officers and clerks within the city, removed the carriage wheels, loaded Baoyin aboard toward the palace city, and several thousand commoners followed empty-handed.
translations.idiomatic: On the day the revolt broke out, former Administrator of South Qiao Wang Lingxiu rushed to Stone City, led the officers and clerks within the city, removed the carriage wheels, loaded Baoyin aboard toward the palace city, and several thousand commoners followed empty-handed.

sentences.zh: 至杜姥宅，日已欲暗，城門閉，城上人射之，眾棄寶寅走。

translations.literal: Reaching Old Woman Du's house, the sun was nearly set; the city gates were closed and men on the walls shot at them; the crowd abandoned Baoyin and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Reaching Old Woman Du's house, the sun was nearly set. The city gates were closed and men on the walls shot at them; the crowd abandoned Baoyin and fled.

sentences.zh: 寶寅逃亡三日，戎服詣草市尉，尉馳以啟帝，帝迎入宮，問之。

translations.literal: Baoyin fled for three days, then came in military dress to the Caoshi market guard; the guard rushed to report to the emperor, who welcomed him into the palace and questioned him.
translations.idiomatic: Baoyin fled for three days, then came in military dress to the Caoshi market guard. The guard rushed to report to the emperor, who welcomed him into the palace and questioned him.

sentences.zh: 寶寅涕泣稱制不自由，帝笑，乃復爵位。

translations.literal: Baoyin wept and said he was not free to act under the system; the emperor laughed and restored his noble rank.
translations.idiomatic: Baoyin wept and said he had not been free to act as he wished. The emperor laughed and restored his noble rank.

sentences.zh: 宣德太后臨朝，改封寶寅鄱陽王。

translations.literal: When Empress Dowager Xuande held court, Baoyin was re-enfeoffed as Prince of Poyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Dowager Xuande held court, Baoyin was re-enfeoffed as Prince of Poyang.

sentences.zh: 中興二年，謀反奔魏。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhongxing he plotted rebellion and fled to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhongxing he plotted rebellion and fled to Wei.

sentences.zh: 邵陵王寶修字智宣，明帝第九子也。

translations.literal: Xiao Baoxiu, Prince of Shaoling, courtesy name Zhixuan, was Emperor Ming's ninth son.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Baoxiu, Prince of Shaoling, courtesy name Zhixuan, was Emperor Ming's ninth son.

sentences.zh: 建武元年，封南平郡王，二年改封。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jianwu he was enfeoffed as Prince of Nanping Commandery; in the second year his enfeoffment was changed.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jianwu he was enfeoffed as Prince of Nanping Commandery; in the second year his enfeoffment was changed.

sentences.zh: 中興二年謀反，宣德太后令賜死。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhongxing he plotted rebellion and Empress Dowager Xuande ordered him granted death.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhongxing he plotted rebellion, and Empress Dowager Xuande ordered him granted death.

sentences.zh: 論曰：守器之重，邦家所馮，觀文惠之在東儲，固已有虧令德，向令負荷斯集，猶當及於禍敗，況先期夙隕，愆失已彰。

translations.literal: Commentary says: The weight of guarding the vessel of state is what the realm relies upon. Observing Wenhui in the Eastern Palace, he already fell short in virtue; had that burden come upon him in full, disaster would still have followed—how much more when he died early and his faults stood revealed.
translations.idiomatic: The commentators say: The weight of guarding the vessel of state is what the realm relies upon. Observing Wenhui in the Eastern Palace, one sees that he already fell short in virtue. Had that burden come upon him in full, disaster would still have followed—how much more when he died early and his faults stood revealed.

sentences.zh: 而武帝不以擇賢，傳之昏孽，推此而論，有冥數矣。

translations.literal: Yet Emperor Wu did not choose the worthy but transmitted the throne to a benighted seed; push the reasoning from this and there is a hidden fate at work.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Emperor Wu did not choose the worthy but transmitted the throne to a benighted heir. Push the reasoning from this and one sees a hidden fate at work.

sentences.zh: 子良物望所集，失在儒雅，當斷不斷，以及於災，非止自致喪亡，乃至宗祀覆滅，哀哉！

translations.literal: Ziliang gathered the admiration of the age; his failure lay in bookish gentleness—when he should have cut clean he did not, and calamity followed. It was not only his own destruction but the overthrow of the ancestral sacrifices. Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Ziliang commanded the admiration of the age, but his failure lay in bookish gentleness—when he should have cut clean he did not, and calamity followed. It was not only his own destruction but the overthrow of the ancestral sacrifices. Alas!

sentences.zh: 夫帝王子弟，生長尊貴，情偽之事，不經耳目，雖卓爾天悟，自得懷抱，孤寡為識，所陋猶多。

translations.literal: Imperial princes and sons are reared in exalted privilege; matters of true and false never pass before their eyes. Though one be singularly gifted by heaven and confident in his own judgment, the views of an isolated and pampered man leave much to be desired.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial princes and sons are reared in exalted privilege; matters of true and false never pass before their eyes. Though one be singularly gifted by heaven and confident in his own judgment, the understanding of an isolated and pampered man leaves much to be desired.

sentences.zh: 齊氏諸王，並幼踐方嶽，故輔以上佐，簡自帝心，勞舊左右，用為主帥，州國府第，先令後行。

translations.literal: All the princes of Qi took up provincial commands while still young; therefore senior administrators were assigned to assist them, chosen from the emperor's own favor and veteran retainers, and made commanders. In the province, state, and mansion, orders went first and action followed after.
translations.idiomatic: All the princes of Qi took up provincial commands while still young. Senior administrators were therefore assigned to assist them, chosen from the emperor's own favor and veteran retainers, and made commanders. In the province, state, and princely mansion, orders went first and action followed after.

sentences.zh: 飲食游居，動應聞啟，端拱守祿，遵承法度，張弛之要，莫敢厝言。

translations.literal: In eating, drinking, travel, and lodging, every move required reporting. Sitting upright and keeping their stipends, they obeyed the law; on the vital points of tightening and loosening authority, none dared set a word amiss.
translations.idiomatic: In eating, drinking, travel, and lodging, every move required reporting. Sitting upright and keeping their stipends, they obeyed the law. On the vital points of tightening and loosening authority, none dared speak out of turn.

sentences.zh: 行事執其權，典簽掣其肘，處地雖重，行止莫由。

translations.literal: Acting governors held the power, chief clerks tugged at their elbows; though their stations were weighty, their comings and goings were not theirs to decide.
translations.idiomatic: Acting governors held the power, chief clerks tugged at their elbows. Though their stations were weighty, their comings and goings were not theirs to decide.

sentences.zh: 威不在身，恩未接下，倉卒一朝，事難總集，望其釋位扶危，不可得矣。

translations.literal: Authority did not rest in their persons; kindness had not reached those below. In a sudden day of crisis, affairs were hard to gather together—to expect them to step down from rank and steady the peril was impossible.
translations.idiomatic: Authority did not rest in their persons, and kindness had not reached those below. In a sudden day of crisis, affairs were hard to gather together—to expect them to step down from rank and steady the peril was impossible.

sentences.zh: 路溫舒云：「秦有十失，其一尚存。

translations.literal: Lu Wenshu said: "Qin had ten failings; one yet remains.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Wenshu said, "Qin had ten failings; one yet remains.

sentences.zh: 」斯宋氏之餘風，及在齊而彌弊。

translations.literal: " This is a remnant of Song custom, which in Qi grew only worse.
translations.idiomatic: This was a remnant of Song custom, which in Qi grew only worse.

sentences.zh: 寶玄親兼一體，欣受家殃，曾不知執柯所指，跗萼相從而敗。

translations.literal: Baoxuan was the emperor's close kin, yet gladly brought ruin on his own house—never knowing who held the axe-handle, never seeing how the flower-stalk withered on the stem.
translations.idiomatic: Baoxuan was the emperor's close kin, yet gladly brought ruin on his own house—never knowing who held the axe-handle, never seeing how calyx and blossom withered together on the stem.

sentences.zh: 以此而圖萬事，未知其髣佛也。

translations.literal: To plan all affairs on such a basis—one cannot even imagine how faintly they understood.
translations.idiomatic: To plan all affairs on such a basis—one cannot even imagine how faintly they understood.
